title: LARP: Language-Agent Role Play for Open-World Games
writing_observation: Contrasts short, bounded agent tasks with persistent open-world demands, then maps that gap onto memory, interaction, and personality components. Its final application expansion is aspirational: the abstract supplies no measured outcomes or comparison supporting the experience claims.

title: Improving Text Embeddings with Large Language Models
writing_observation: Leads with a compact efficiency claim, then contrasts pipeline complexity with synthetic task diversity. The mechanism is unusually concrete, while separate unlabeled and mixed-data result statements keep the performance claims tied to different supervision settings.

title: DocLLM: A layout-aware generative language model for multimodal document understanding
writing_observation: Opens with the need to combine document text and layout, then explains bounding-box attention and infilling. Evidence closes with dataset-level win counts and unseen-set coverage, making the scope more concrete than a generic superiority claim.

title: LLaMA Beyond English: An Empirical Study on Language Capability Transfer
writing_observation: The abstract turns English-dominant pretraining into a concrete transfer question, then inventories interventions and evaluation dimensions. Compute expenditure signals study scale, while the strongest evidence is data efficiency; named benchmarks and thirteen languages bound the empirical reach.

title: Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models
writing_observation: Frames improvement without additional human annotations, explains iterative self-generated contrastive training, and separates theoretical and empirical support. Named benchmarks clarify evaluation scope, while the final human-level aspiration extends beyond the abstract's quantified evidence.

title: Understanding LLMs: A Comprehensive Overview from Training to Inference
writing_observation: The survey motivates organization through training and deployment cost, then enumerates a lifecycle taxonomy. Its contribution is synthesis across preprocessing, optimization, compression, and serving; this structure should not be evaluated using a new-method abstract template.

title: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation
writing_observation: A table-top limitation motivates whole-body mobile imitation, followed by a clear hardware-to-data-to-learning sequence. Demonstration count and vivid household tasks make the result concrete; the maximum success-rate gain lacks an explicit baseline denominator or typical-effect description.

title: TinyLlama: An Open-Source Small Language Model
writing_observation: TinyLlama leads with model scale, training volume, and architectural lineage, then positions efficiency and size-matched benchmark comparisons as evidence. Its abstract is a compact resource report; the opening spends less space on an unresolved scientific gap.

title: LLM Augmented LLMs: Expanding Capabilities through Composition
writing_observation: A cost-of-adaptation problem motivates composition instead of retraining. Cross-attention provides the central mechanism, followed by an enumerated feature list; named base models and task-specific gains anchor the claim, although frozen weights are rhetorically equated with capability preservation.

title: LLaMA Pro: Progressive LLaMA with Block Expansion
writing_observation: LLaMA Pro motivates adaptation through catastrophic forgetting, specifies which added parameters are trained, and names code and mathematics as the study domains. A sharper version would replace broad superiority language with explicit benchmark and retention measurements.

title: DocGraphLM: Documental Graph Language Model for Information Extraction
writing_observation: The abstract positions its contribution between transformer and graph approaches, then enumerates representation and reconstruction components. Direction, distance, and neighborhood weighting give the mechanism specificity; the evidence remains broad, with unnamed datasets and unquantified accuracy and convergence gains.

title: DeepSeek LLM: Scaling Open-Source Language Models with Longtermism
writing_observation: Uses disagreement about scaling laws as the opening gap, then organizes the contribution around model sizes, data volume, and post-training stages. Named comparator wins supply direction, but absent score magnitudes leave the empirical support comparatively coarse.

title: Blending Is All You Need: Cheaper, Better Alternative to Trillion-Parameters LLM
writing_observation: Introduces the cost of model scaling and turns it into an explicit research question. The blending proposal is simple; model sizes, deployment platform, and thirty-day testing period give context, although outcome magnitudes remain unspecified.

title: MoE-Mamba: Efficient Selective State Space Models with Mixture of Experts
writing_observation: MoE-Mamba connects two established research directions and makes their combination the hypothesis. It grounds the benefit in equal-performance training steps while separately preserving inference advantages, a useful separation of training efficiency from deployment claims.

title: Mixtral of Experts
writing_observation: Introduces the model directly rather than opening with a gap paragraph. Architecture details make sparse activation concrete, followed by named comparator families and task categories. Parameter counts specify the efficiency story; benchmark superiority is asserted without effect sizes.

title: MagicVideo-V2: Multi-Stage High-Aesthetic Video Generation
writing_observation: Moves quickly from demand to a four-component pipeline, favoring architectural inventory over an explicit failure diagnosis. Named commercial comparators ground its conclusion, but the user-study claim lacks sample size, effect magnitude, and a stated operating boundary.

title: Masked Audio Generation using a Single Non-Autoregressive Transformer
writing_observation: The abstract is mechanism-first and clearly separates masked-token training from iterative inference. Rescoring and hybrid generation precede evaluation, which combines objective and human evidence; the quantified speedup and explicit quality–latency tradeoffs make the conclusion comparatively bounded.

title: PIXART-δ: Fast and Controllable Image Generation with Latent Consistency Models
writing_observation: The report opens directly with an integration claim rather than a research gap. Resolution, sampling steps, latency, hardware, training time, and memory make deployment benefits tangible; controllability appears as a second contribution with less quantitative support.

title: TrustLLM: Trustworthiness in Large Language Models
writing_observation: Moves from a broad trust concern to enumerated principles, benchmark dimensions, and model counts. Its numbered findings include exceptions and over-refusal, showing how an evaluation abstract can present favorable trends alongside a consequential boundary.

title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
writing_observation: Defines expert specialization before naming two architectural interventions, making the proposed mechanism legible. Successive model scales and computation ratios provide concrete evidence, although the preliminary largest-scale claim and tentative percentage weaken the otherwise precise conclusion.

title: Transformers are Multi-State RNNs
writing_observation: Begins with a conceptual reframing of transformers as recurrent models, then derives cache compression as a practical consequence. TOVA supplies the algorithmic contribution. Long-range experiments and an explicit cache fraction support efficiency, while 'nearly on par' remains imprecise.

title: PALP: Prompt Aligned Personalization of Text-to-Image Models
writing_observation: PALP makes the personalization–prompt-alignment tradeoff concrete, then acknowledges that optimizing for one prompt narrows the setting. The mechanism follows that concession, and quantitative plus qualitative comparisons support usefulness within the restricted scope.

title: InstantID: Zero-shot Identity-Preserving Generation in Seconds
writing_observation: Two competing method families receive distinct limitation lists before the proposal appears. The abstract explains IdentityNet through conditioning choices and names compatible models, but relies on strong evaluative adjectives rather than quantified fidelity, efficiency, or application evidence.

title: Contrastive Preference Optimization: Pushing the Boundaries of LLM Performance in Machine Translation
writing_observation: Sets up a named translation-performance gap, diagnoses imperfect reference supervision, and introduces preference optimization as the response. Training-data and parameter quantities establish economy; named annual test sets bound the comparison, though improvement magnitudes are omitted.

title: Scalable Pre-training of Large Autoregressive Image Models
writing_observation: AIM states two explicit scaling findings before presenting a large-scale demonstration. Frozen-backbone ImageNet performance serves as the measurable consequence, while continued scaling is framed as an observation rather than a proof of unlimited improvement.

title: Vision Mamba: Efficient Visual Representation Learning with Bidirectional State Space Model
writing_observation: Connects visual position and context requirements to bidirectional state-space design. Named tasks establish breadth; speed and memory claims include a concrete resolution and comparator, demonstrating how resource claims gain meaning from explicitly stated conditions.

title: VMamba: Visual State Space Model
writing_observation: Builds its motivation through a concrete CNN–Transformer complexity tradeoff, then derives the design from global receptive fields and dynamic weights. The cross-scan intervention addresses a named obstacle; the closing evidence remains qualitative despite a clear resolution-dependent boundary.

title: ChatQA: Building GPT-4 Level Conversational QA Models
writing_observation: ChatQA introduces model quality first, then separates instruction tuning from retrieval adaptation. The final comparison specifies ten datasets and an average score while identifying excluded synthetic-data sources, making the claimed parity more interpretable than an unqualified GPT-4 comparison.

title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
writing_observation: Connects a hardware bottleneck to the maintenance burden of a separate draft model. Parallel heads and tree verification provide the mechanism; two tuning regimes clarify tradeoffs. Reported speedup ranges give concrete evidence while distinguishing frozen from jointly trained backbones.

title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
writing_observation: The opening explicitly relocates contribution from novel modules to data scaling. Two numbered strategies organize the mechanism, and named evaluation settings establish breadth; universal-sounding motivation exceeds the bounded evidence described, whose gains lack numeric magnitudes.

title: Spotting LLMs With Binoculars: Zero-Shot Detection of Machine-Generated Text
writing_observation: Challenges an assumed detection difficulty before introducing a two-model contrast score. The no-training requirement is repeated as a useful constraint. Detection rate paired with a very low false-positive rate provides an interpretable operating point, bounded by evaluated document sources.

title: Large Language Models are Superpositions of All Characters: Attaining Arbitrary Role-play via Self-Alignment
writing_observation: Recasts role-play improvement as activating existing model knowledge rather than copying proprietary systems. Self-generated dialogues and fine-tuning operationalize that premise. Dataset scale and named evaluations define coverage, while cross-supervision separates transferable style from limits in role-specific knowledge.

title: Lumiere: A Space-Time Diffusion Model for Video Generation
writing_observation: The abstract leads with the motion-coherence problem, then contrasts whole-video generation with keyframe interpolation. Architectural operations explain the proposed advantage; the closing application list broadens relevance, while performance claims remain unquantified and limitations are absent.

title: Meta-Prompting: Enhancing Language Models with Task-Agnostic Scaffolding
writing_observation: Meta-Prompting explains orchestration through a conductor-and-experts analogy before giving the actual decomposition and verification sequence. Its quantitative ending specifies tasks and competing prompting baselines, though the long mechanism description could be compressed for a conference abstract.

title: MM-LLMs: Recent Advances in MultiModal Large Language Models
writing_observation: Uses a survey roadmap instead of a method-problem-result arc: architectural formulation, catalog of 26 systems, benchmark review, training recipes, and future directions. Its concrete evidence of scope is coverage count, with no experimental improvement claim of its own.

title: Scaling Up to Excellence: Practicing Model Scaling for Photo-Realistic Image Restoration In the Wild
writing_observation: Leads with the system and scaling opportunity, then lists training scale, textual control, and fidelity-oriented sampling. The dataset size is specific, but restoration improvements remain qualitative; persuasive adjectives carry more weight than comparative effect sizes.

title: MambaByte: Token-free Selective State Space Model
writing_observation: MambaByte states the benefit of removing tokenization, immediately introduces the resulting sequence-length cost, and presents selective state spaces as the response. Comparative efficiency and downstream quality jointly support a narrowly scoped viability claim.

title: Diffuse to Choose: Enriching Image Conditioned Inpainting in Latent Diffusion Models for Virtual Try-All
writing_observation: Builds motivation from virtual shopping, then contrasts detail preservation against inference speed. The proposed feature injection and perceptual loss address that tradeoff explicitly. Evaluation spans private and public data, but superiority lacks dataset names and effect sizes.

title: WebVoyager: Building an End-to-End Web Agent with Large Multimodal Models
writing_observation: Identifies two linked evaluation gaps: single-modality agents and unrealistic web settings. The response combines an agent, a 15-site benchmark, and an automatic evaluator. Task success and human-judge agreement quantify distinct contributions instead of conflating agent quality with evaluator validity.

title: DeepSeek-Coder: When the Large Language Model Meets Programming -- The Rise of Code Intelligence
writing_observation: Frames restricted access to strong code models as the research obstacle, then specifies corpus scale, model sizes, and infilling pretraining. Named closed and open comparators anchor the evaluation claim, although the abstract gives no numerical accuracy gains.

title: SliceGPT: Compress Large Language Models by Deleting Rows and Columns
writing_observation: A resource bottleneck leads to a precise criticism of sparse representations, followed by smaller dense matrices as the mechanism. Named models, retained performance, and hardware-specific compute figures make evidence concrete; the enabling invariance insight arrives unusually late.

title: From GPT-4 to Gemini and Beyond: Assessing the Landscape of MLLMs on Generalizability, Trustworthiness and Causality through Four Modalities
writing_observation: Explicitly labels the study qualitative and bounds its scope with modalities, model counts, cases, and a score matrix. The abstract advertises fourteen findings without exemplifying one, so evaluation design is more specific than its substantive takeaway.

title: MoE-LLaVA: Mixture of Experts for Large Vision-Language Models
writing_observation: Opens with the cost of scaling dense vision-language models and links sparse routing to that bottleneck. A separate tuning strategy addresses multimodal sparsity degradation. Active-parameter counts and named dense comparators sharpen the evidence, while hallucination improvements remain unquantified.

title: Motion-I2V: Consistent and Controllable Image-to-Video Generation with Explicit Motion Modeling
writing_observation: Contrasts direct video generation with a two-stage motion decomposition, explaining how predicted trajectories guide temporal attention. Control and translation extensions follow the mechanism; the evidence statement promises quantitative and qualitative comparisons without reporting numerical effects.

title: Rephrasing the Web: A Recipe for Compute and Data-Efficient Language Modeling
writing_observation: Connects noisy web data to both compute and quality constraints before describing a simple rephrasing intervention. Fixed-budget results and task counts sharpen the evidence; its closing causal attribution is stronger than the abstract's abbreviated experimental explanation.

title: InternLM-XComposer2: Mastering Free-form Text-Image Composition and Comprehension in Vision-Language Large Model
writing_observation: Starts with composition capability rather than a sharply stated research gap, then motivates image-token-specific adaptation through language preservation. It names model size and strong comparators, but restricts equivalence to some assessments without numerical effects.

title: BlockFusion: Expandable 3D Scene Generation using Latent Tri-plane Extrapolation
writing_observation: Leads with expandable scene generation and devotes most space to the representation, compression, and overlapping-block extrapolation pipeline. It explains controllability and indoor/outdoor scope, while comparative quality remains asserted without named metrics or baselines.

title: Weaver: Foundation Models for Creative Writing
writing_observation: Presents a specialized model family, then explains corpus selection, writer alignment, and size-dependent routing. Evaluation is tied to a curated writing benchmark and named competitor, but no measured margin or assessment reliability appears in the abstract.

title: YOLO-World: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
writing_observation: YOLO-World moves from closed-category limitations to named architectural and loss changes, then reports accuracy and speed together with dataset and hardware. The evaluation sentence ties open-vocabulary capability to practical operating conditions rather than an isolated quality score.

title: Jamba: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model
writing_observation: Leads with an architectural contribution and explains the function of each hybrid component. GPU memory and context-length numbers make feasibility tangible. Benchmark claims are broad, but ablations and configuration-specific language signal that design choices and implementation scope matter.

title: Transformer-Lite: High-efficiency Deployment of Large Language Models on Mobile Phone GPUs
writing_observation: Moves from mobile latency to four enumerated engineering changes, each tied to an implementation bottleneck. Model sizes and processor compatibility define scope. Separate prefill and decoding rates, plus named comparator speedups, make the performance claim more interpretable than one aggregate acceleration number.

title: Gecko: Versatile Text Embeddings Distilled from Large Language Models
writing_observation: Introduces the artifact immediately, then uses an ordered two-step account to explain synthetic data generation and relabeling. Embedding dimensions, a named benchmark, and size ratios make compactness concrete, though the abstract offers little explicit problem or limitation discussion.

title: Aurora-M: The First Open Source Multilingual Language Model Red-teamed according to the U.S. Executive Order
writing_observation: Combines accessibility, multilingual coverage, forgetting, and safety into a model-release rationale. Training lineage, languages, and token counts make the intervention concrete. Evaluation is described broadly, so the claimed multilingual and safety advantages are less precisely bounded than the training recipe.

title: Octopus v2: On-device language model for super agent
writing_observation: Octopus v2 motivates local function calling through privacy, cost, latency, and accuracy, then emphasizes resource and performance gains. The abstract leaves the proposed mechanism and evaluated workload largely unspecified; those omissions caution against copying its promotional compression.

title: Long-context LLMs Struggle with Long In-context Learning
writing_observation: LIConBench motivates a measurement gap between synthetic long-context tests and label-intensive learning. Its abstract describes dataset and model coverage, reports a context-length boundary, and uses positional bias analysis to explain the observed degradation.

title: Advancing LLM Reasoning Generalists with Preference Trees
writing_observation: Eurus leads with benchmark outcomes, then attributes the contribution to a structured preference dataset and a new objective. Its abstract connects preference-tree components to the training use cases while distinguishing general conversation alignment from reasoning-specific requirements.

title: Mixture-of-Depths: Dynamically allocating compute in transformer-based language models
writing_observation: The opening states a precise inefficiency, then explains dynamic token routing under a fixed total budget. Static tensor shapes resolve an apparent implementation objection before results appear; matched training budgets and a bounded sampling-speed figure strengthen the efficiency argument.

title: Language Models as Compilers: Simulating Pseudocode Execution Improves Algorithmic Reasoning in Language Models
writing_observation: Narrows algorithmic reasoning difficulty to generating reusable logic rather than instance-specific executable code. A two-stage task-level pseudocode and execution framework makes the intervention legible. Seven tasks and named reasoning baselines support scope, though the abstract omits numerical improvement magnitudes.

title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
writing_observation: Defines the central change as next-scale prediction instead of raster ordering, then substantiates generation claims with named metrics, benchmark resolution, and speed. Scaling and transfer claims broaden the conclusion, while concrete task names maintain some boundaries.

title: ReFT: Representation Finetuning for Language Models
writing_observation: Derives representation adaptation from an interpretability-based hypothesis before distinguishing the family from a concrete low-rank instance. Efficiency ratios and evaluation counts give specificity, while 'almost always' usefully qualifies the broad performance claim without identifying the exceptions.

title: CoMat: Aligning Text-to-Image Diffusion Model with Image-to-Text Concept Matching
writing_observation: Frames the gap as an unexplained alignment failure, then chains a token-attention diagnosis to caption-based feedback and attribute binding. Training-data restrictions are concrete; the broad root-cause language is stronger than the abstract's unquantified two-benchmark evidence.

title: Direct Nash Optimization: Teaching Language Models to Self-Improve with General Preferences
writing_observation: Explains the limitation through cyclic preferences before positioning the algorithm between contrastive simplicity and preference generality. A named model, benchmark, response-length control, and before–after win rates make the empirical conclusion unusually inspectable alongside the theoretical claim.

title: MagicTime: Time-lapse Video Generation Models as Metamorphic Simulators
writing_observation: Organizes a crowded method around three numbered components and a purpose-built dataset, each tied to metamorphic motion. The physical-knowledge premise carries the narrative, while the closing simulator ambition is appropriately suggestive but supported only by unspecified experimental superiority.

title: Ferret-UI: Grounded Mobile UI Understanding with Multimodal LLMs
writing_observation: Ferret-UI links elongated screens and small interface objects to a concrete resolution adaptation. The abstract then separates elementary grounding data, advanced reasoning data, and evaluation, providing a clear chain from domain-specific obstacles to the experimental design.

title: Eagle and Finch: RWKV with Matrix-Valued States and Dynamic Recurrence
writing_observation: Introduces two successor architectures and ties state structure and recurrence to expressivity and inference efficiency. Corpus size and model scales are explicit; competitive benchmark performance is summarized broadly without numerical comparisons or a detailed gap statement.

title: LLM2Vec: Large Language Models Are Secretly Powerful Text Encoders
writing_observation: LLM2Vec turns a perceived architecture mismatch into a three-step transformation. Evaluation distinguishes word-level from sequence-level tasks and unsupervised from supervised settings, illustrating how to prevent different supervision regimes from blurring a headline comparison.

title: OmniFusion Technical Report
writing_observation: Presents a design-space comparison rather than a sharply isolated research gap. The list of adapters, encoders, tiling options, and benchmarks conveys coverage, but its best-configuration claim gives no margin and the application catalogue extends beyond that quantified scope.

title: InternLM-XComposer2-4KHD: A Pioneering Large Vision-Language Model Handling Resolutions from 336 Pixels to 4K HD
writing_observation: The abstract quantifies the prior resolution ceiling before introducing a wider operating range and its patch-allocation mechanism. Acknowledging that maximum resolution is not always needed adds practical nuance; benchmark-count comparisons provide breadth without showing effect sizes or failure cases.

title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
writing_observation: Challenges the validity of a popular retrieval proxy, then explains richer synthetic task categories. Model and task counts plus a context-length threshold make the diagnostic result concrete, while the term satisfactory would need an operational definition.

title: Leave No Context Behind: Efficient Infinite Context Transformers with Infini-attention
writing_observation: Infini-attention states a resource-bounded streaming objective and then names the local, compressed-memory, and long-term components. Finite retrieval and summarization experiments support the implementation; they should remain distinct from the theoretical claim about arbitrarily long input streams.

title: JetMoE: Reaching Llama2 Performance with 0.1M Dollars
writing_observation: Uses cost as the motivating gap and headline evidence, then explains sparse attention and feedforward experts as the mechanism. Training tokens, accelerator-hours, active parameters, and a compute reduction make efficiency auditable; quality comparisons name models without listing benchmark-specific gains.

title: Best Practices and Lessons Learned on Synthetic Data for Language Models
writing_observation: Frames synthetic data around scarcity, privacy, and acquisition cost, then offers a research overview rather than a new generation method. Its evidence is explicitly prior work. Factuality, fidelity, and bias are presented as conditions on utility rather than guaranteed outcomes.

title: RecurrentGemma: Moving Past Transformers for Efficient Open Language Models
writing_observation: This unusually compact abstract moves directly from artifact introduction to architecture, memory rationale, released variants, and a named comparator. Parameter count supplies scope, but comparative performance and fewer training tokens remain qualitative, with no benchmark, effect size, or limitation.

title: Rho-1: Not All Tokens Are What You Need
writing_observation: Challenges uniform token weighting, uses training-dynamics observations to motivate selective loss, and explains reference-model scoring. Multiple numerical outcomes distinguish math and general-domain settings, although peak improvement language requires care about its narrower scope.

title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
writing_observation: Moves from restricted existing environments to a concrete executable benchmark, specifying task count and reproducibility machinery. A numerical human–agent gap establishes difficulty, and named failure categories connect aggregate results to a useful research agenda.

title: Ferret-v2: An Improved Baseline for Referring and Grounding with Large Language Models
writing_observation: A predecessor's limitations anchor the gap, followed by three explicitly numbered upgrades. Each design has a stated purpose, making the contribution easy to scan; however, substantial comparative gains and their attributed causes are asserted without abstract-level numerical or ablation evidence.

title: ControlNet++: Improving Conditional Controls with Efficient Consistency Feedback
writing_observation: ControlNet++ connects control mismatch to a cycle-consistency objective, then explains the memory problem created by a naive implementation and its single-step solution. Task-specific metrics at the end support controllability across different conditional inputs.

title: Pre-training Small Base LMs with Fewer Tokens
writing_observation: The recipe is explained before motivation, using a concise inherit-then-train sequence. Data fraction, model sizes, hardware, time, and benchmark count supply unusually concrete scope; a second experimental setting distinguishes token-efficient construction from matching larger-model validation loss.

title: Megalodon: Efficient LLM Pretraining and Inference with Unlimited Context Length
writing_observation: The abstract establishes a two-sided gap: transformers scale poorly, while efficient alternatives lose performance. It then lists architectural changes and a controlled comparison with precise model scale, token budget, and losses; the unlimited-context claim receives less direct abstract-level evidence.

title: TransformerFAM: Feedback attention is working memory
writing_observation: Compresses problem, feedback mechanism, and compatibility into a short causal narrative. Named model sizes supply experimental scope, but repeated unlimited-length language reaches beyond the unspecified task lengths and unquantified improvements reported in the abstract.

title: Learn Your Reference Model for Real Good Alignment
writing_observation: Builds the gap through an explanatory history from RLHF regularization to DPO's fixed reference. Updating that reference is presented as a simple correction. Named datasets and GPT-4 evaluation bound the reported gain, although 'up to' highlights a best-case result.

title: Dynamic Typography: Bringing Words to Life
writing_observation: Motivates automation through the expertise required for meaningful animated lettering. It decomposes the visual objective into semantic deformation, motion, and legibility, then connects each to modeling constraints. Qualitative and quantitative evaluations are promised without named datasets or effect sizes.

title: Toward Self-Improvement of LLMs via Imagination, Searching, and Criticizing
writing_observation: Develops a two-stage gap: scarce supervision motivates self-improvement, but unreliable self-correction motivates search and critics. The components track stated obstacles well; evidence is bounded to mathematical reasoning, despite the broader opening language about planning.

title: Reka Core, Flash, and Edge: A Series of Powerful Multimodal Language Models
writing_observation: Reka's abstract organizes a model family by compute class and modality, then combines automatic benchmarks with blinded human judgments. It distinguishes named model variants and evaluation settings; qualitative availability is asserted without replacing the need for a documented sampling procedure.

title: AutoCrawler: A Progressive Understanding Web Agent for Web Crawler Generation
writing_observation: The abstract motivates its task through separate failures of wrappers and generative agents, then specifies a two-stage HTML-based framework. Named top-down and corrective operations explain behavior; the concluding evaluation claim lacks datasets, numerical gains, and explicit operating boundaries.

title: Groma: Localized Visual Tokenization for Grounding Multimodal Large Language Models
writing_observation: Groma's abstract makes localization part of visual tokenization, connecting region-level inputs and grounded outputs through one mechanism. Dataset curation and comparisons against alternative localization locations follow, keeping the architectural distinction central to the empirical story.

title: FlowMind: Automatic Workflow Generation with LLMs
writing_observation: FlowMind links unpredictable workflow demands to API-grounded prompting, then adds inspectable workflow descriptions and a finance benchmark. The evaluation promises baseline, component, and interaction studies, while confidentiality claims require explicit threat and access assumptions beyond the abstract.

title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
writing_observation: The abstract moves from attack classes to a specific hypothesized vulnerability, then pairs a behavioral hierarchy with training-data generation. Naming GPT-3.5 and unseen attacks scopes the evidence, but robustness gains and capability costs are described without numbers.

title: How Good Are Low-bit Quantized LLaMA3 Models? An Empirical Study
writing_observation: Frames compression as a deployment question about a newly released model family. The evaluation scope is specific in method count and bit range; the main contribution is a negative finding, although degradation magnitudes are not supplied.

title: Phi-3 Technical Report: A Highly Capable Language Model Locally on Your Phone
writing_observation: Opens with model size, training scale, named comparators, and benchmark scores, making the practical claim immediately testable. It explicitly locates novelty in data and labels larger-model findings initial, although deployment feasibility receives no hardware measurement in the abstract.

title: OpenELM: An Efficient Language Model Family with Open-source Training and Inference Framework
writing_observation: Motivates transparent research before introducing layer-wise parameter allocation. A size-matched accuracy comparison and token budget give concrete evidence, while enumerated logs, checkpoints, and configurations turn the openness contribution into specific deliverables.

title: Pegasus-v1 Technical Report
writing_observation: Positions the work as a technical report on video comprehension, naming temporal challenges and evaluation families. It explicitly promises qualitative limitations as well as capabilities, but leaves the architectural mechanism and measured outcomes unspecified.

title: FlashSpeech: Efficient Zero-Shot Speech Synthesis
writing_observation: States a clear quality-versus-speed problem, then explains consistency training and a prosody module. Sampling-step and speed claims make the efficiency story concrete; comparable quality remains unquantified and the comparison conditions are deferred.

title: Multi-Head Mixture-of-Experts
writing_observation: Enumerates two specific mixture-of-experts weaknesses and mirrors them with token splitting and parallel expert processing. The mechanism is easy to map to motivation; evidence spans three task families but gives neither benchmark names nor effect sizes.

title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
writing_observation: The abstract uses a numbered training–inference–decoding progression, explaining how early exits and later verification share computation. It closes with task-specific maximum speedups and model-training breadth, but leaves accuracy tradeoffs and memory reductions largely unquantified.

title: Make Your LLM Fully Utilize the Context
writing_observation: A named failure mode leads to an explicitly labeled causal hypothesis and a data-based intervention. Training requirements and diagnostic tasks are concrete; paired before–after numbers for long- and short-context tasks communicate benefit and retained capability without hiding the slight short-task decline.

title: How Far Are We to GPT-4V? Closing the Gap to Commercial Multimodal Models with Open-Source Suites
writing_observation: States an open-versus-proprietary capability gap and packages the response into three numbered improvements. Concrete tiling and resolution details distinguish the recipe from a vague model release. Winning eight of eighteen benchmarks provides an explicit boundary to the performance claim.

title: PLLaVA : Parameter-free LLaVA Extension from Images to Videos for Video Dense Captioning
writing_observation: Uses a failed straightforward adaptation as the pivot from motivation to diagnosis, then explains pooling as the corrective mechanism. Two benchmark-specific results substantiate the proposal, although percentage comparisons could state more clearly whether differences are relative or absolute.

title: Replacing Judges with Juries: Evaluating LLM Generations with a Panel of Diverse Models
writing_observation: Explains why model-based judging became necessary before isolating cost and self-family bias in single-judge practice. A diverse panel is a direct response. Three settings, six datasets, and a cost ratio specify breadth and efficiency, without quantifying the agreement improvement.

title: Unveiling Encoder-Free Vision-Language Models
writing_observation: The abstract develops its gap in stages: encoder constraints, the appeal of removal, and observed failure of direct training. Two remedies organize the contribution, while public-data scale supports transparency; comparative adjectives and criticism of another model substitute for quantitative result details.

title: HuatuoGPT-Vision, Towards Injecting Medical Visual Knowledge into Multimodal LLMs at Scale
writing_observation: A data-quality bottleneck is traced to privacy, annotation expense, and residual noise. The abstract then links denoising to dataset scale, expert checks, benchmark improvements, and a trained model; concrete artifact sizes contrast with unquantified performance and quality claims.

title: TabReD: A Benchmark of Tabular Machine Learning in-the-Wild
writing_observation: Explains two concrete mismatches between academic datasets and deployment: time variation and engineered features. Eight industry datasets instantiate the solution. Ranking changes under temporal splits make the benchmark's value observable, with model conclusions appropriately restricted to this collection.

title: ROS-LLM: A ROS framework for embodied AI with task feedback and structured reasoning
writing_observation: Centers the beneficiary—nonexpert robot programmers—and describes integration, behavior representations, learning, and feedback. Evaluation scenarios establish application breadth, but robustness and scalability are stated without quantitative definitions or comparative measurements.

title: Scaling Synthetic Data Creation with 1,000,000,000 Personas
writing_observation: Leads with persona-driven synthesis and a billion-persona resource, making scale the main novelty cue. Use-case enumeration substitutes for benchmark deltas. Broad claims about coverage and paradigm change exceed the concrete evidence described, offering a useful example of scope needing tighter qualification.

title: We-Math: Does Your Large Multimodal Model Achieve Human-like Mathematical Reasoning?
writing_observation: Identifies a limitation in end-to-end math scores, then introduces concept decomposition and diagnostic categories as the benchmark's mechanism. Dataset size and concept hierarchy specify coverage. Findings distinguish knowledge deficits from generalization failures, although causal interpretations require more support than the abstract provides.

title: Summary of a Haystack: A Challenge to Long-Context LLMs and RAG Systems

writing_observation: Grounds the retrieval gap in specific visual document cues, introduces a benchmark, then motivates the image-based architecture from that gap. title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents

writing_observation: OpenVid-1M pairs two identified gaps, accessible high-quality video data and insufficient textual conditioning, with separate dataset and architecture contributions. title: InternLM-XComposer-2.5: A Versatile Large Vision Language Model Supporting Long-Contextual Input and Output
writing_observation: InternLM-XComposer-2.5 presents version-specific upgrades and separates comprehension from composition extensions. writing_observation: Conflicting experiences with synthetic data motivate quality and diversity as the bottleneck. title: MJ-Bench: Is Your Multimodal Reward Model Really a Good Judge for Text-to-Image Generation?

title: Multimodal Self-Instruct: Synthetic Abstract Image and Visual Reasoning Instruction Using Language Model
writing_observation: Uses everyday visual tasks to make an abstract-image capability gap tangible, then separates benchmark construction from a fine-tuning validation. title: Inference Performance Optimization for Large Language Models on CPUs

title: PaliGemma: A versatile 3B VLM for transfer
writing_observation: The abstract prioritizes artifact identity and transfer purpose over a conventional gap narrative. Named vision and language backbones establish composition, while nearly forty tasks communicate breadth; performance remains qualitative and the brief text does not explain training choices or limitations.

title: LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave: Tackling Multi-image, Video, and 3D in Large Multimodal Models

title: Skywork-Math: Data Scaling Laws for Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models -- The Story Goes On

title: Video Diffusion Alignment via Reward Gradients
writing_observation: Identifies video-data collection as an adaptation bottleneck and motivates differentiable reward signals as a sample-efficient alternative. The mechanism-to-benefit link is clear; multiple models support breadth, but efficiency gains have no numerical magnitude.

writing_observation: Uses a failed serialization baseline to make token limits tangible, then maps the remedy to three compression modules. Quantified detection and compression results anchor the contribution; downstream question answering broadens scope without a similarly detailed outcome.

title: Human-like Episodic Memory for Infinite Context LLMs

title: Qwen2 Technical Report

writing_observation: Qwen2-Audio explains two user interaction modes and a simplified prompting scheme before its benchmark comparison. title: NeedleBench: Can LLMs Do Retrieval and Reasoning in 1 Million Context Window?

title: GoldFinch: High Performance RWKV/Transformer Hybrid with Linear Pre-Fill and Extreme KV-Cache Compression

title: Spectra: A Comprehensive Study of Ternary, Quantized, and FP16 Language Models

title: E5-V: Universal Embeddings with Multimodal Large Language Models
writing_observation: The abstract frames embedding adaptation as an underexplored use of multimodal models, then highlights the counterintuitive choice of text-only training. title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
writing_observation: AgentPoison frames an agent-specific trust-boundary weakness and distinguishes external-memory poisoning from model retraining. title: CoD, Towards an Interpretable Medical Agent using Chain of Diagnosis
writing_observation: Motivates diagnostic interpretability and explains chained reasoning, confidence distributions, and entropy-based inquiry. title: Scaling Laws with Vocabulary: Larger Models Deserve Larger Vocabularies
writing_observation: The abstract identifies an omitted scaling variable, enumerates three convergent analyses, and separates a large-model prediction from smaller-model validation. title: LazyLLM: Dynamic Token Pruning for Efficient Long Context LLM Inference

title: EVLM: An Efficient Vision-Language Model for Visual Understanding
writing_observation: Identifies two distinct shortcomings of a common architecture and follows with a numbered design response. title: KAN or MLP: A Fairer Comparison

writing_observation: Lists scalability, diversity, and management as separate platform gaps, then maps each to an infrastructure or usability component. writing_observation: Moves from disease burden directly to a tri-modal classification architecture, specifying features and GPT-4's text-processing role. writing_observation: Leads with model sizes and domain specialization, then organizes adaptation into three explicit stages. Corpus scale and a named legal benchmark provide scope, while superiority and trade-off claims lack numerical outcomes in the abstract.

title: SeaLLMs 3: Open Foundation and Chat Multilingual Large Language Models for Southeast Asian Languages
writing_observation: SeaLLMs 3 motivates an underserved-language gap, names its language coverage, and links tailored training data to resource efficiency. title: FreeLong: Training-Free Long Video Generation with SpectralBlend Temporal Attention
writing_observation: Motivates training-free extension through resource constraints, then inserts a diagnostic observation before proposing frequency blending. title: Theia: Distilling Diverse Vision Foundation Models for Robot Learning
writing_observation: The motivation connects robot control to the need for diverse visual knowledge, making multi-teacher distillation a natural mechanism. writing_observation: Enumerates retrieval, noise, and context-capacity challenges before assigning planner and searcher roles to a graph-based workflow. Page count and elapsed time convey scale; human preference comparisons are named, but their margins and the human-time estimate lack detail.

writing_observation: Frames a language-specific resource contribution through model size, corpus scale, adaptation lineage, and a knowledge cutoff. It distinguishes base and instruction models and ends with licensing; evaluation is mentioned without scores, leaving capability strength unspecified.

title: OS-Genesis: Automating GUI Agent Trajectory Construction via Reverse Task Synthesis
writing_observation: Establishes data collection as the bottleneck and makes reversal of task–trajectory order the central explanatory idea. A reward model closes the quality-control loop; performance and diversity claims remain qualitative despite the detailed procedural contrast.

title: 2.5 Years in Class: A Multimodal Textbook for Vision-Language Pretraining
writing_observation: Names three deficiencies in web interleaving and answers them with a video-derived corpus construction sequence. writing_observation: States a two-part difficulty—identity preservation and coherent motion—then maps global identity, box trajectories, and pixel warping to different control levels. writing_observation: Introduces a world-representation model, data engine, and action head as a connected system. writing_observation: STAR motivates temporal inconsistency and fidelity loss as distinct obstacles in video restoration. title: REINFORCE++: A Simple and Efficient Approach for Aligning Large Language Models

title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
writing_observation: Uses a compact conceptual definition of policy and world models to motivate a developer platform. It inventories curation, pretrained models, post-training examples, and tokenizers; the abstract is release-oriented and contains no measured evaluation outcome.

writing_observation: Separates high-level visual-language reasoning from precise spatial manipulation and explains why fine-tuning is costly. writing_observation: Motivates an end-to-end research assistant through cost and time, specifies three workflow stages, and describes researcher participation. title: rStar-Math: Small LLMs Can Master Math Reasoning with Self-Evolved Deep Thinking

writing_observation: Enumerates three challenges and answers them with a staged dataset, reward-model, and reinforcement-learning pipeline. title: Enhancing Human-Like Responses in Large Language Models

writing_observation: Connects reasoning errors to missing knowledge and retrieved-document noise. Dynamic search and a separate document-analysis stage map cleanly to those two problems. title: LlamaV-o1: Rethinking Step-by-step Visual Reasoning in LLMs
writing_observation: Packages the response to weak step-level visual reasoning as a benchmark, a metric, and a curriculum-trained model. Category and reasoning-step counts establish scope. A named comparator, average score, absolute gain, and speed ratio make the empirical claim concrete.

title: Transformer^2: Self-adaptive LLMs

writing_observation: Connects a breadth-and-access gap to an extraction framework, then validates the resource through released models. title: The Lessons of Developing Process Reward Models in Mathematical Reasoning

writing_observation: Makes long context the organizing advantage, linking attention, experts, and parallel execution before reporting scale. title: GameFactory: Creating New Games with Generative Interactive Videos

title: MangaNinja: Line Art Colorization with Precise Reference Following
writing_observation: Starts directly with the specialized task and links two named designs to correspondence and controllability. A self-collected benchmark and challenging use cases establish scope, but broad superiority language is not accompanied by sample counts or quantitative effect sizes.

title: Hunyuan3D 2.0: Scaling Diffusion Models for High Resolution Textured 3D Assets Generation
writing_observation: Organizes a release around two named components for geometry and texture, followed by a production platform. Evaluation dimensions are explicit, but comparative superiority lacks metrics or effect sizes; the motivation is partly an open-resource gap.

writing_observation: UI-TARS specifies a screenshot-to-action interface, names benchmark interaction budgets, and then enumerates perception, action-space, reasoning, and iterative-data contributions. title: SRMT: Shared Memory for Multi-agent Lifelong Pathfinding

title: Envisioning Beyond the Pixels: Benchmarking Reasoning-Informed Visual Editing
writing_observation: The abstract converts general editing difficulties into four reasoning categories and three evaluation dimensions. Human and model judging, nine evaluated systems, and a named best-model score make the benchmark argument concrete; test-set size and judging agreement are not specified.

title: Rethinking Reflection in Pre-Training
writing_observation: The abstract corrects a temporal assumption about when reflection emerges, then defines a direct intervention using deliberately corrupted reasoning. Tracking pretraining checkpoints supports the developmental claim, while a named model, token budget, and six tasks provide scope without quantified effect sizes.

title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
writing_observation: Contrasts attention inefficiency with limited recurrent-state expressivity, motivating trainable neural hidden states. A cartoon dataset and human Elo comparison make the proof of concept concrete. Explicit artifacts, implementation limitations, and one-minute resource constraints give unusually clear boundaries to the conclusion.

title: SmolVLM: Redefining small and efficient multimodal models
writing_observation: Makes inefficient inheritance from larger models the specific gap, rather than small size alone. Memory measurements and model-scale contrasts reinforce the deployment story; acknowledging the older comparator's development gap adds context to an otherwise dramatic performance comparison.

title: Skywork R1V: Pioneering Multimodal Reasoning with Chain-of-Thought
writing_observation: Introduces lightweight visual adaptation, then separates alignment optimization from adaptive reasoning-length distillation. Named visual and text benchmark scores make the capability claim concrete; efficiency benefits are asserted without corresponding latency or compute measurements.

title: DDT: Decoupled Diffusion Transformer
writing_observation: Builds the mechanism from a stated conflict between semantic encoding and detail reconstruction. Decoupling encoder and decoder resolves that proposed tension. ImageNet resolutions, FID values, and convergence speed quantify evidence; a separate reuse strategy explains an additional inference-efficiency benefit.

title: An Empirical Study of GPT-4o Image Generation Capabilities
writing_observation: A brief historical progression motivates an empirical question about unified generation, followed by four categories and more than twenty tasks. The abstract promises strengths and limitations but reports neither concrete findings nor metrics, leaving architecture-related conclusions weakly connected to visible evidence.

title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
writing_observation: Motivates parallel reasoning through limitations of predefined collaboration frameworks, then details shared-cache workers and positional-embedding support. The key outcome is feasibility without fine-tuning; the abstract supplies no measured speedup or quality trade-off.

title: OmniSVG: A Unified Scalable Vector Graphics Generation Model
writing_observation: Contrasts expensive or oversimplified SVG generation with discrete-token modeling that separates structure from geometry. Dataset scale and an evaluation protocol constitute additional contributions; the abstract gives no numerical improvement despite naming the practical design target.

title: OLMoTrace: Tracing Language Model Outputs Back to Trillions of Training Tokens
writing_observation: Introduces output-to-training-data tracing with an explicit verbatim-match definition, separating the observable operation from possible applications. Corpus scale and response time are concrete; hallucination and creativity are exploratory use cases rather than validated diagnostic guarantees.

title: DeepSeek-R1 Thoughtology: Let's <think> about LLM Reasoning
writing_observation: Uses publicly visible reasoning traces to motivate a taxonomy-led analysis rather than a new model. The finding sequence highlights overthinking, repetitive exploration, and safety vulnerabilities. Its nuanced conclusions are memorable, but datasets, sample sizes, and quantitative effect sizes are unspecified.

title: Kimi-VL Technical Report
writing_observation: Kimi-VL distinguishes active decoder capacity, input resolution, context length, and a later reasoning variant. Its task-specific numerical results clarify coverage, while the dense catalog of capabilities would need prioritization when adapted to a shorter conference contribution.

title: C3PO: Critical-Layer, Core-Expert, Collaborative Pathway Optimization for Test-Time Expert Re-Mixing
writing_observation: Starts from a measured routing gap and turns it into sample-specific test-time optimization. Neighbor-based surrogates explain how optimization proceeds without test labels; restricted layers and experts address cost. Two models, six benchmarks, and improvement ranges provide concrete empirical scope.

title: Seaweed-7B: Cost-Effective Training of Video Generation Foundation Model
writing_observation: Treats the model as evidence for a cost-efficient training strategy. Parameter count and accelerator-hours provide concrete resource scope; design decisions are emphasized without enumerating them. Comparisons with larger models and downstream adaptation are claimed broadly, lacking named benchmarks or improvement magnitudes.

title: PRIMA.CPP: Speeding Up 70B-Scale LLM Inference on Low-Resource Everyday Home Clusters
writing_observation: Defines an unusually concrete deployment setting before explaining scheduling and overlap mechanisms. Hardware count, model sizes, latency, throughput, and comparators make evidence operational; the final hardware-independent wording is broader than the four-device setup described.

title: InternVL3: Exploring Advanced Training and Test-Time Recipes for Open-Source Multimodal Models
writing_observation: InternVL3 makes joint multimodal pretraining the organizing distinction, then lists context, post-training, and inference additions. The abstract's concrete MMMU result anchors broad capability claims, but separate ablations are needed to attribute gains among the combined recipe changes.

title: xVerify: Efficient Answer Verifier for Reasoning Model Evaluations
writing_observation: xVerify defines two evaluation failures, answer extraction and equivalence checking, before presenting the verifier and labeled dataset. Its evidence separates held-out/generalization accuracy from downstream reward-model utility, avoiding reliance on one intrinsic metric.

title: Seedream 3.0 Technical Report
writing_observation: Organizes improvements across data, pretraining, post-training, and deployment, tying them to predecessor limitations. Speedup and output-resolution numbers are specific; aesthetic and typography improvements lack comparable measured effects in the abstract.

title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
writing_observation: Progresses from tool-suited reasoning failures to explicit interaction and training stages. Accuracy and training-step comparisons are unusually concrete, while the extended setting is separately labeled; the 'aha moment' interpretation is more anthropomorphic than the observable self-correction evidence.

title: BitNet b1.58 2B4T Technical Report
writing_observation: Opens as a model release with precision, parameter count, and token count, followed by capability coverage and deployment artifacts. The matched-size comparison gives useful scope, but memory, energy, and latency advantages receive no magnitudes in the abstract.

title: Antidistillation Sampling
writing_observation: States a sharply focused threat and intervention with little preamble, making the objective immediately legible. The sampling mechanism is described only at the distribution level, and claims of preserved utility and impaired distillation lack experimental conditions or measurements.

title: CLIMB: CLustering-based Iterative Data Mixture Bootstrapping for Language Model Pre-training
writing_observation: The abstract motivates mixture optimization through missing domain labels and costly manual curation. Semantic clustering, proxy evaluation, and iterative search form a coherent mechanism; model and corpus scales plus comparative gains add specificity, though percentage units and evaluation metrics remain underspecified.

title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
writing_observation: The abstract challenges a prevailing interpretation, then makes evaluation choice central to the argument. Contrasting small- and large-sample pass rates explains the surprising finding; model, algorithm, and task breadth support scope, while repeated references to current RLVR settings constrain generalization.

title: Learning to Reason under Off-Policy Guidance
writing_observation: An on-policy learning constraint motivates mixing external demonstrations with self-generated rollouts. The abstract combines an algorithmic explanation, a convergence claim, and benchmark gains; its strongest concluding language is broader than the stated experiments, and theorem assumptions remain outside the abstract.

title: Kuwain 1.5B: An Arabic SLM via Language Injection
writing_observation: Frames language addition as preserving prior knowledge, then supplies a small-model instance and an average improvement. The efficiency motivation is clear, but 'injection' remains underspecified and retention, benchmark identities, and resource savings are not numerically documented.

title: Eagle 2.5: Boosting Long-Context Post-Training for Frontier Vision-Language Models
writing_observation: Eagle 2.5 links long-video context and image detail preservation to two named training operations and a multilevel annotation dataset. The benchmark comparison includes frame budget and model size, helping readers assess the resource context of the reported quality.

title: VisuLogic: A Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Reasoning in Multi-modal Large Language Models
writing_observation: Identifies language shortcuts as a measurement-validity problem, then specifies benchmark size, categories, and verification. Model scores are anchored against random and human baselines, producing a clear diagnostic takeaway rather than relying solely on dataset scale.

title: Towards Understanding Camera Motions in Any Video
writing_observation: Introduces a benchmark through a taxonomy and expert annotation process, using a zoom-versus-translation example to make the difficulty concrete. Contrasting geometric and semantic failures motivates model adaptation. Dataset scale is specified, but numerical performance gains are absent from the abstract.

title: The Bitter Lesson Learned from 2,000+ Multilingual Benchmarks
writing_observation: The multilingual benchmarking position paper states its corpus scope, then uses geographic coverage and human-alignment correlations to motivate recommendations. Its rhetorical strength is connecting proposed principles to measured disparities rather than presenting a taxonomy without consequences.

title: Describe Anything: Detailed Localized Image and Video Captioning
writing_observation: Links localized captioning errors to the need for both detail and global context. Two architectural components address representation, while semi-supervised data and a reference-free benchmark address training and evaluation. Seven benchmark families establish breadth, though the abstract gives no score deltas.

title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
writing_observation: A precise missing-label problem motivates majority-vote reward estimation and test-time learning. The abstract names a model, benchmark, metric, and large relative gain, but omits the absolute starting score; comparisons to initial voting and label-supervised training frame the claimed improvement.

title: Skywork R1V2: Multimodal Hybrid Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning
writing_observation: Explains a hybrid objective and selective sampling as responses to reasoning and optimization problems. It also reports a harmful training effect and mitigation; multiple named benchmark scores strengthen evidence despite an expansive superiority framing.

title: Paper2Code: Automating Code Generation from Scientific Papers in Machine Learning
writing_observation: PaperCoder motivates unavailable implementations and describes a dependency-aware planning, analysis, and generation pipeline. Evaluation includes model judgments and original-author assessment, linking code faithfulness to multiple evidence sources rather than treating executable output alone as successful reproduction.

title: Step1X-Edit: A Practical Framework for General Image Editing
writing_observation: Motivates an open model through the gap to proprietary editing systems, then outlines multimodal interpretation followed by diffusion decoding. Data construction and a user-instruction benchmark complete the contribution package. Competitive results are asserted without numerical margins, so evaluation specificity is limited.

title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
writing_observation: Connects persistent-dialogue inconsistency to three memory operations and a graph extension, then carefully enumerates comparator categories. Relative quality gains, p95 latency, and token costs make the tradeoff concrete, though the broad deployment conclusion rests on one named benchmark.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning in Large Language Models with One Training Example
writing_observation: The one-example RLVR study opens with a surprising minimal-data claim, then carefully distinguishes overall gains from format correction. Cross-model, cross-algorithm, and mechanism analyses strengthen the narrative beyond a single favorable example or benchmark.

title: UniversalRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Multiple Corpora with Diverse Modalities and Granularities
writing_observation: Identifies modality-restricted retrieval as the gap and introduces routing through an observed representation bias. Granularity and theoretical justification deepen the method account; ten benchmarks bound the evaluation, but comparative gains are unquantified.

title: The Leaderboard Illusion
writing_observation: The abstract builds an argument through multiple mechanisms of benchmark distortion, supporting each with concrete counts or estimated shares. It distinguishes estimates and maximum gains, acknowledges the platform's value, and closes with reform proposals rather than treating criticism as the only contribution.

title: Ovis-U1 Technical Report
writing_observation: Frames unified understanding, generation, and editing as the contribution, then contrasts joint training with frozen-model alternatives. A decoder and token refiner specify the mechanism. Named benchmarks and scores across all three capabilities provide balanced evidence instead of relying on a single flagship result.

title: Thinking with Images for Multimodal Reasoning: Foundations, Methods, and Future Frontiers
writing_observation: The thinking-with-images survey organizes a field through increasing visual autonomy rather than only model categories. It makes principles, methods, evaluation, and future questions separate contributions, but cognition analogies should remain explanatory framing rather than empirical proof.

title: Does Math Reasoning Improve General LLM Capabilities? Understanding Transferability of LLM Reasoning
writing_observation: Turns a popular progress metric into a transfer question, first surveying models and then using controlled tuning comparisons. Representation analyses support the proposed explanation; the abstract clearly distinguishes broad observational results from narrower intervention evidence.

title: Should We Still Pretrain Encoders with Masked Language Modeling?
writing_observation: The encoder-pretraining study explicitly identifies scale as a confounder and uses controlled ablations to separate objectives. Its mixed findings motivate a staged training strategy, demonstrating a strong observation-to-method narrative under a fixed compute budget.

title: GLM-4.1V-Thinking: Towards Versatile Multimodal Reasoning with Scalable Reinforcement Learning
writing_observation: The report introduces a model family and presents pretraining followed by curriculum-based reinforcement learning as its development logic. Benchmark counts and size-matched comparisons convey breadth, but the long capability list and expanded release inventory crowd out quantified gains or explicit failure boundaries.

title: Skywork-Reward-V2: Scaling Preference Data Curation via Human-AI Synergy
writing_observation: Skywork-Reward-V2 states a data-quality hypothesis before describing human-guided curation and a model family. Its abstract distinguishes raw dataset scale from the training subset and promises ablations separating quantity from quality, strengthening attribution of reward-model gains.

title: LongAnimation: Long Animation Generation with Dynamic Global-Local Memory
writing_observation: Derives a global-memory need from the failure of local segment smoothing, then explains component responsibilities and inference refinement. Explicit short- and long-sequence lengths make the evaluation boundary visible, although the abstract reports effectiveness without a measured gain.

title: Kwai Keye-VL Technical Report
writing_observation: Contrasts static-image competence with short-video difficulty, then explains data scale and staged reasoning training. The abstract names a new benchmark and behavioral corrections, but performance superiority is unquantified despite detailed recipe descriptions.

title: Test-Time Scaling with Reflective Generative Model
writing_observation: Leads with a competitor-level performance claim, then enumerates shared-backbone scoring and outcome-supervised rewards. Parameter overhead and controllable reasoning modes give mechanism detail, while comparison evidence omits benchmark names and numerical scores.

title: Energy-Based Transformers are Scalable Learners and Thinkers
writing_observation: Energy-Based Transformers turns a generalization question about inference-time computation into a compatibility-based optimization mechanism. Evidence spans modalities and distinguishes training scaling from inference gains, though broad claims require careful baseline and compute accounting across those settings.

title: WebSailor: Navigating Super-human Reasoning for Web Agent
writing_observation: Frames a proprietary-versus-open capability gap around uncertainty reduction, then describes task construction, cold start, and reinforcement learning as a unified recipe. The benchmark context is recognizable, but performance matching and superhuman language are not accompanied by scores or bounded comparison conditions.

title: MemOS: A Memory OS for AI System
writing_observation: Develops a systems gap across persistent knowledge and lifecycle control, then defines a concrete memory unit with provenance and versioning. The unification proposal is clear, but the abstract is architectural positioning rather than an empirical demonstration of cost or learning benefits.

title: Open Vision Reasoner: Transferring Linguistic Cognitive Behavior for Visual Reasoning
writing_observation: The abstract turns cross-modal transfer into a two-stage training recipe, then presents three interpretive findings before benchmark scores. Named architecture, training duration, and task-specific accuracies create specificity; claims about mental imagery and behavioral mechanisms are stronger than the abstract's described tests.

title: SingLoRA: Low Rank Adaptation Using a Single Matrix
writing_observation: Explains the two-matrix baseline before replacing it with a single-matrix construction, making simplicity intelligible. The theory's infinite-width setting provides scope and numerical examples add specificity, though the abstract's description of MNLI as commonsense reasoning creates a task-label ambiguity.

title: T-LoRA: Single Image Diffusion Model Customization Without Overfitting
writing_observation: A narrow single-image setting makes the overfitting problem concrete, and a timestep-dependent observation motivates the proposed adaptation rule. Two enumerated innovations organize the method; named diffusion backbones and component evaluations support scope, but the claimed tradeoff improvement lacks numbers.

title: OmniPart: Part-Aware 3D Generation with Semantic Decoupling and Structural Cohesion
writing_observation: Motivates editable parts through the limitations of monolithic generation, then explains planning and simultaneous synthesis as complementary stages. Control interfaces and output structure are clear; state-of-art performance remains unquantified in the abstract.

title: Skywork-R1V3 Technical Report
writing_observation: Frames visual reasoning as transfer from text models and identifies reinforcement learning, connector alignment, and checkpoint selection as mechanisms. A named benchmark's before-and-after scores provide concrete support, though human-level framing requires evaluation context beyond the abstract.

title: A Survey on Latent Reasoning
writing_observation: Frames tokenized reasoning as an expressive bottleneck, then organizes the survey from foundational computation to methods and advanced paradigms. This is a conceptual roadmap rather than a results abstract; coverage boundaries and literature-selection criteria are not specified.

title: Gemini 2.5: Pushing the Frontier with Advanced Reasoning, Multimodality, Long Context, and Next Generation Agentic Capabilities
writing_observation: Uses a product-family structure rather than a research-gap narrative, assigning different capability-cost roles to each model. Three-hour video capacity is concrete. The Pareto-frontier and state-of-the-art claims are broad, with no benchmark scores or training mechanism supplied in the abstract.

title: 4KAgent: Agentic Any Image to 4K Super-Resolution
writing_observation: Leads with a broad restoration promise, then makes the system intelligible through profiling, perception, and execution roles. Eleven task categories, twenty-six benchmarks, and named metric families specify coverage. Universal applicability and clinical-image implications still require stronger boundaries than the abstract states.

title: MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents
writing_observation: Explains the proposed memory taxonomy and gives two distinctly scoped evaluations with concrete storage and accuracy figures. However, sweeping claims about solving memory and ensuring privacy are rhetorically stronger than the benchmark evidence and local-storage description establish.

title: Scaling RL to Long Videos
writing_observation: Uses a full-stack contribution structure: dataset, training procedure, and distributed infrastructure. Dataset size, video length, named benchmark scores with subtitle conditions, and training speedup quantify different aspects. Hardware-specific feasibility statements help bound the otherwise broad long-video scaling claim.

title: Vision Foundation Models as Effective Visual Tokenizers for Autoregressive Image Generation
writing_observation: Opens with an underexplored frozen-encoder design and enumerates two additions that target redundancy and semantics. A named generation metric, convergence factor, and absence of guidance make the result more concrete than generic efficiency language.

title: NeuralOS: Towards Simulating Operating Systems via Neural Generative Models
writing_observation: Describes the input-output contract first, then assigns state tracking and image generation to separate components. Training data and concrete state-transition examples establish the setting. Synthetic application demonstrations motivate broader possibilities, while evidence remains qualitative and limited to the described operating-system environment.

title: Towards Agentic RAG with Deep Reasoning: A Survey of RAG-Reasoning Systems in LLMs
writing_observation: Complementary weaknesses in retrieval and reasoning motivate a bidirectional taxonomy, followed by a third category for their iterative integration. The survey roadmap is coherent and application-focused; collection scope, inclusion criteria, and evidence behind broad performance claims remain unstated.

title: Mixture-of-Recursions: Learning Dynamic Recursive Depths for Adaptive Token-Level Computation
writing_observation: Mixture-of-Recursions names parameter sharing and adaptive computation as two distinct efficiency targets, then explains routing and cache behavior. The evaluation uses matched training FLOPs and multiple model sizes, supporting a tradeoff-based claim rather than isolated speedup.

title: Reasoning or Memorization? Unreliable Results of Reinforcement Learning Due to Data Contamination
writing_observation: Builds a research puzzle from surprising reward findings that fail to transfer across model families. Contamination becomes the alternative explanation, tested with generated arithmetic tasks. The conclusion narrows valid reward claims and explicitly recommends clean benchmarks and cross-model checks.

title: The Devil behind the mask: An emergent safety vulnerability of Diffusion LLMs
writing_observation: Connects an architectural distinction to a specific safety-evaluation gap, then explains why the proposed probe targets that distinction. Separate keyword, evaluator, and rejection metrics improve specificity, while repeated 'up to' framing leaves average vulnerability and variability unstated.

title: EXAONE 4.0: Unified Large Language Models Integrating Non-reasoning and Reasoning Modes
writing_observation: Defines the release through two operating modes, language coverage, and two deployment-oriented model sizes. The capability inventory is easy to follow, but comparative performance remains categorical because benchmarks, scores, and the relevant model-class boundaries are absent.

title: A Survey of Context Engineering for Large Language Models
writing_observation: The context-engineering survey distinguishes foundational operations from integrated system types and identifies output-generation asymmetry as a research gap. The stated paper count describes coverage, not reading depth or representativeness; a survey must document its selection and synthesis method.

title: π^3: Scalable Permutation-Equivariant Visual Geometry Learning
writing_observation: Identifies dependence on a reference view as a concrete failure source, then makes permutation equivariance the architectural remedy. Output invariances are specified; named task families establish breadth, but no numerical accuracy or robustness effects appear.

title: VisionThink: Smart and Efficient Vision Language Model via Reinforcement Learning
writing_observation: A concrete asymmetry between OCR and general visual questions motivates adaptive resolution rather than uniform compression. The request-token mechanism is easy to visualize, and reinforcement learning explains its training; final efficiency claims lack measured savings despite the detailed problem setup.

title: nablaNABLA: Neighborhood Adaptive Block-Level Attention
writing_observation: NABLA gives a direct quadratic-attention bottleneck, an adaptive block-sparsity response, and an integration path through an existing operator. Its speed claim is paired with several quality measures, encouraging efficiency reporting that includes implementation accessibility and output degradation.

title: NoHumansRequired: Autonomous High-Quality Image Editing Triplet Mining
writing_observation: The abstract derives a data-mining problem from precise edit-quality requirements, then explains validation and compositional expansion. Dataset size, expansion factor, and stage-wise survival analysis make production scale tangible; broad cross-dataset superiority is less specific than the resource and pipeline claims.

title: MiroMind-M1: An Open-Source Advancement in Mathematical Reasoning via Context-Aware Multi-Stage Policy Optimization
writing_observation: Reproducibility, rather than a pure accuracy gap, anchors the motivation. Explicit dataset sizes, sequential training stages, and a named optimization mechanism support the openness claim; model families and benchmarks bound comparisons, although accuracy and token-efficiency gains remain qualitative.

title: The Invisible Leash: Why RLVR May Not Escape Its Origin
writing_observation: Poses a precise question about capability expansion versus redistribution, then distinguishes first-sample accuracy from wider sampling support. Token-level and answer-level entropy separate misleading proxies; conclusions are qualified as potential limits rather than universal impossibility.
