title: GUI-G^2: Gaussian Reward Modeling for GUI Grounding
writing_observation: Starts with a precisely defined task and reward mismatch, then explains point, coverage, and scale-adaptive mechanisms. Benchmark names and the largest gain give evidence, although emphasizing a maximum leaves typical gains unclear and the closing paradigm claim broad.

title: Deep Researcher with Test-Time Diffusion
writing_observation: Turns the diffusion analogy into an operational draft-and-retrieval loop, giving the metaphor explanatory value. The additional self-evolution component is less specified, and the concluding state-of-the-art claim names neither benchmarks nor numerical improvements.

title: Step-Audio 2 Technical Report
writing_observation: Introduces an audio system through encoder, reinforcement-learning, token-generation, and retrieval components, connecting each to understanding or conversational behavior. Training volume conveys scale. The final benchmark-superiority claim lacks named tests, numerical outcomes, and detailed comparison conditions in the abstract.

title: Beyond Context Limits: Subconscious Threads for Long-Horizon Reasoning
writing_observation: TIM separates a recursively trained model from its runtime and explains memory reuse through a reasoning-tree representation. The abstract links throughput and task performance to the system, while effectively unlimited context remains a claim requiring clear resource and dependency assumptions.

title: MegaScience: Pushing the Frontiers of Post-Training Datasets for Science Reasoning
writing_observation: MegaScience presents a data gap, a textbook-derived dataset, and a larger mixture as separate objects. Selection ablations and a multi-benchmark evaluation system connect dataset construction to training efficiency, answer extraction, and model-scale transfer.

title: Pixels, Patterns, but No Poetry: To See The World like Humans
writing_observation: The abstract challenges a common compensatory assumption and develops a structural explanation through timing and representation-space distinctions. A purpose-built test anchors the critique, but task counts, model comparisons, and effect sizes are absent; forceful terminology heightens the burden of evidence.

title: Yume: An Interactive World Generation Model
writing_observation: Distinguishes an ambitious future vision from the preview's image-and-keyboard scope, then lists four generation and acceleration components. The technical recipe is detailed, but scene diversity and visual-quality outcomes remain unquantified.

title: Group Sequence Policy Optimization
writing_observation: Introduces an algorithm directly and distinguishes it through the unit of likelihood ratios and clipping. Stability and efficiency are tied to a named baseline and mixture-of-experts training. The compact abstract offers no benchmark scores, variance measures, or compute conditions.

title: Agentic Reinforced Policy Optimization
writing_observation: Uses post-tool uncertainty as an empirical observation motivating adaptive rollout and stepwise attribution. Benchmark count and a halved tool budget support breadth and efficiency, while exact task-wise gains and accounting conditions are deferred.

title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: On Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
writing_observation: Uses a what–when–how taxonomy to organize a broad survey and enumerates components, adaptation stages, and feedback types. That structure is memorable, while the closing superintelligence ambition extends well beyond the review scope and evidence described.

title: BANG: Dividing 3D Assets via Generative Exploded Dynamics
writing_observation: An intuitive human-design analogy motivates controllable object decomposition, followed by a named generative process and concrete adapter, attention, and prompting components. The closing application cascade broadens appeal, but no explicit evaluation protocol, quantitative result, or failure boundary supports it.

title: HunyuanWorld 1.0: Generating Immersive, Explorable, and Interactive 3D Worlds from Words or Pixels
writing_observation: HunyuanWorld contrasts video and explicit-3D approaches, then ties a layered mesh representation to immersion, exportability, and interaction. The abstract's application breadth is clearer than its evaluation specifics, which need measurable definitions of coherence and interactive utility.

title: Falcon-H1: A Family of Hybrid-Head Language Models Redefining Efficiency and Performance
writing_observation: Explains a parallel attention-state-space hybrid through the goal of balancing capability and efficiency. Model variants, language coverage, and context length define the release. Named larger comparators make claims recognizable, but training-data and performance advantages lack benchmark-level numbers in the abstract.

title: ScreenCoder: Advancing Visual-to-Code Generation for Front-End Automation via Modular Multimodal Agents
writing_observation: The abstract attributes complex-UI failures to overloaded monolithic processing, then mirrors that diagnosis with grounding, planning, and generation agents. A second data-generation contribution feeds model training; the causal narrative is clear, but performance and robustness claims lack benchmarks or quantified evidence.

title: MCPMark: A Benchmark for Stress-Testing Realistic and Comprehensive MCP Use
writing_observation: MCPMark makes interaction depth and mutable environments the benchmark gap, then defines initial states and programmatic verification. Its abstract reports both one-shot success and repeated reliability alongside tool-call counts, showing why agent evaluation needs more than task accuracy.

title: DeepSearch: Overcome the Bottleneck of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Monte Carlo Tree Search
writing_observation: Attributes reinforcement-learning plateaus to sparse exploration, then contrasts training-time search with inference-only use. Three contributions specify search and replay design; average accuracy and GPU-hour savings substantiate results, though the benchmark mixture is unnamed.

title: Vision-Zero: Scalable VLM Self-Improvement via Strategic Gamified Self-Play
writing_observation: Vision-Zero connects annotation cost to label-free visual games and separates arbitrary-image game generation from the iterative training algorithm. Its three-part contribution structure clarifies the proposed route to generalization, while sustained-improvement claims require trajectories beyond final benchmark results.

title: The Dragon Hatchling: The Missing Link between the Transformer and Models of the Brain
writing_observation: Opens with a biological-computational analogy, then presents architectural, empirical, and interpretability arguments separately. Matched parameter/data comparisons to GPT-2 specify performance scope. Claims about brain plausibility and concept-specific synapses are stronger than the abstract's quantitative evidence, so their interpretation needs care.

title: LongCodeZip: Compress Long Context for Code Language Models
writing_observation: Motivates compression through API cost and latency, then identifies code structure as the weakness in general text pruning. Function-level and block-level selection make the mechanism concrete. Several code tasks and a maximum compression ratio support utility, though worst-case quality boundaries are unstated.

title: GEM: A Gym for Agentic LLMs
writing_observation: Motivates an environment interface for experience-based learning, then describes execution, extensibility, and training integration. Baseline coverage and matched algorithm comparisons define the contribution; the abstract emphasizes infrastructure and analysis rather than a superiority score.

title: ExGRPO: Learning to Reason from Experience
writing_observation: A specific wasteful training practice motivates a question about which experiences deserve reuse. Correctness and entropy provide the bridge from analysis to algorithm, while model-count, size range, and separate benchmark gains make evidence concrete; training-stability claims broaden the empirical payoff.

title: Self-Forcing++: Towards Minute-Scale High-Quality Video Generation
writing_observation: Self-Forcing++ motivates degradation beyond a short teacher's horizon and describes segment-based guidance from self-generated videos. Its length claims distinguish ordinary extension from higher-compute generation, and fidelity plus consistency are separate evaluation targets rather than one visual-quality label.

title: Cache-to-Cache: Direct Semantic Communication Between Large Language Models
writing_observation: Turns the information loss and latency of text-based coordination into a direct research question. Oracle evidence motivates cache projection, fusion, and layer gating. Accuracy gains against individual models and text communication are separated from latency, clarifying which baseline supports each claim.

title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
writing_observation: Names two concrete failure modes of context rewriting before introducing incremental playbook updates, yielding a clear problem–mechanism link. Aggregate gains and a harder benchmark split sharpen the evidence, while the possibility wording around unsupervised adaptation appropriately limits that claim.

title: When Models Lie, We Learn: Multilingual Span-Level Hallucination Detection with PsiloQA
writing_observation: The abstract defines two benchmark deficiencies—coarse labels and English restriction—then provides a three-stage construction process and language count. Evaluated detector families make the empirical comparison legible; annotation reliability, transfer magnitudes, and claimed cost savings are not quantified.

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
writing_observation: Tiny Recursive Model motivates simplification of a specific predecessor, then reports architecture size and puzzle performance. The abstract's compactness is effective, but parameter comparisons against general-purpose language models must remain scoped to the evaluated task and training regime.

title: Paper2Video: Automatic Video Generation from Scientific Papers
writing_observation: Defines presentation-video generation as coordinated scientific communication, motivating a paired dataset and four task-specific metrics. It then introduces a multi-agent system; dataset count is concrete, while faithfulness and informativeness gains lack numerical comparison.

title: In-the-Flow Agentic System Optimization for Effective Planning and Tool Use
writing_observation: AgentFlow names the mismatch between modular agents and offline optimization, then places planner training inside live interaction. The abstract explains credit assignment and reports task-family gains, supporting a method story that joins system decomposition with a training objective.

title: D2E: Scaling Vision-Action Pretraining on Desktop Data for Transfer to Embodied AI
writing_observation: Motivates alternative training data through collection cost, distinguishes prior work by scope and openness, and enumerates a complete pipeline. Data-hour composition and named success rates provide specificity, though the final real-world transfer phrasing needs the benchmark conditions for interpretation.

title: MM-HELIX: Boosting Multimodal Long-Chain Reflective Reasoning with Holistic Platform and Adaptive Hybrid Policy Optimization
writing_observation: Uses a benchmark diagnosis to motivate both new training data and a reward-aware optimization strategy. Dataset sizes, baseline identity, and separate in-benchmark versus general-task gains create a coherent evidence chain; the broad generalization conclusion remains tied to those tested categories.

title: Agent Learning via Early Experience
writing_observation: The abstract motivates an intermediate learning paradigm through missing rewards, costly rollouts, and narrow expert coverage. Future states provide a clear supervision mechanism, with two named strategies; eight environments bound empirical breadth, while later reinforcement-learning benefits are cautiously described as promising signals.

title: Thinking with Camera: A Unified Multimodal Model for Camera-Centric Understanding and Generation
writing_observation: Identifies separately studied camera understanding and generation as the gap, then unifies them through a camera-as-language representation. Four million triplets and explicit parameter/map inputs define training scope. Generalization examples are concrete, but comparative performance lacks numerical support in the abstract.

title: DITING: A Multi-Agent Evaluation Framework for Benchmarking Web Novel Translation
writing_observation: DITING defines genre-specific translation dimensions, distinguishes the evaluation dataset from a metric-validation subset, and tests automatic judgments against humans. This creates a coherent benchmark–evaluator–meta-evaluation chain rather than treating a new judge's scores as self-validating.

title: KORMo: Korean Open Reasoning Model for Everyone
writing_observation: Positions openness and synthetic-data viability as the contribution, with an unusually precise synthetic share and training origin. Two enumerated findings provide focus, but near-native language and stability claims lack operational metrics or explicit evaluation magnitudes in the abstract.

title: Diffusion Transformers with Representation Autoencoders
writing_observation: The abstract isolates a neglected component and lists three concrete weaknesses before proposing representation-based autoencoding. It acknowledges the new high-dimensional challenge rather than skipping it; guidance-specific FID numbers ground results, while recommending a new default exceeds the listed evaluation scope.

title: Scaling Language-Centric Omnimodal Representation Learning
writing_observation: Begins with an explanatory gap in embedding success, then connects latent alignment analysis to a lightweight refinement framework. A proposed scaling relationship links empirical findings and theory. The low-resource retrieval test narrows validation, while broad state-of-the-art claims lack numerical detail.

title: QeRL: Beyond Efficiency -- Quantization-enhanced Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
writing_observation: Combines a resource bottleneck with an unexpected exploration benefit of quantization, then introduces adaptive noise. Hardware, model sizes, rollout speedup, and named benchmark scores give concrete evidence, while component speed and total training cost are distinguished.

title: Spatial Forcing: Implicit Spatial Representation Alignment for Vision-language-action Model
writing_observation: Builds a layered gap by explaining both 2D limitations and the costs of explicit or estimated depth. The alignment mechanism directly answers those constraints; simulation and real-world scope are named, but the headline speedup is a maximum without operating conditions.

title: RAG-Anything: All-in-One RAG Framework
writing_observation: RAG-Anything motivates fragmented multimodal evidence and connects a dual-graph representation to hybrid retrieval. The abstract identifies long documents as a relevant regime, but broad all-modality and superiority wording would benefit from named settings, metrics, and limitations.

title: Robot Learning: A Tutorial
writing_observation: Frames a field transition rather than a missing algorithm and clearly identifies the intended audience. Its roadmap moves from reinforcement learning and cloning to language-conditioned generalists. Ready-to-use examples substantiate practical value; the abstract appropriately avoids claiming new experimental superiority.

title: Advancing End-to-End Pixel Space Generative Modeling via Self-supervised Pre-training
writing_observation: States a pixel-versus-latent training gap and gives a two-stage encoder-pretraining and end-to-end refinement mechanism. Resolution-specific FID, function evaluations, and relative training compute make evidence unusually explicit. Diffusion and consistency outcomes are reported separately, preserving distinct contribution scopes.

title: PaddleOCR-VL: Boosting Multilingual Document Parsing via a 0.9B Ultra-Compact Vision-Language Model
writing_observation: Leads with a compact document parser and identifies its visual and language backbones. Parameter size, language count, and document elements establish scope; public and internal evaluations are mentioned, but speed and superiority remain unquantified.

title: Agentic Entropy-Balanced Policy Optimization
writing_observation: Identifies entropy-driven exploration as a potential collapse mechanism and splits the remedy across rollout and policy updates. Dataset and baseline counts plus separate sampling-budget scores provide unusually specific evaluation context for the claimed training stability.

title: WithAnyone: Towards Controllable and ID Consistent Image Generation
writing_observation: Names a concrete copying failure and traces it to scarce paired identity data. Dataset, benchmark, and contrastive training form a coherent three-part response; evaluation covers fidelity–variation trade-offs, although neither effect sizes nor user-study counts appear.

title: A Theoretical Study on Bridging Internal Probability and Self-Consistency for LLM Reasoning
writing_observation: RPC uses confidence-estimation errors to distinguish self-consistency and perplexity weaknesses, then derives two complementary remedies. The abstract links theoretical convergence, confidence reliability, and sampling cost, making assumptions and comparison budgets central to assessing the headline claim.

title: OmniVinci: Enhancing Architecture and Data for Omni-Modal Understanding LLM
writing_observation: Separates architecture innovations from data curation, then gives modality-specific improvements and a training-token comparison. This makes breadth and efficiency concrete; downstream application claims are less evidenced than the named benchmarks and the opening human-sensing analogy.

title: DeepAnalyze: Agentic Large Language Models for Autonomous Data Science
writing_observation: The abstract contrasts predefined workflows with end-to-end autonomy, then introduces curriculum training and grounded trajectory synthesis. An 8B model size sharpens the comparison with proprietary-model agents, but the strongest autonomy and superiority claims lack named benchmarks, numerical results, or failure conditions.

title: FineVision: Open Data Is All You Need
writing_observation: Motivates dataset unification through fragmentation and contamination, then makes curation auditable through source counts, human checks, deduplication, and benchmark screening. Comparative training outcomes are stated broadly; data-process specificity carries more evidence than effect-size reporting.

title: Efficient Long-context Language Model Training by Core Attention Disaggregation
writing_observation: Opens with an exact computational object, then derives disaggregation from statelessness and composability. Scheduling, overlap, hardware count, and maximum context length make the systems contribution concrete; the throughput gain is explicitly bounded as a maximum.

title: DeepSeek-OCR: Contexts Optical Compression
writing_observation: The abstract labels the work an initial feasibility investigation, then reports a compression–accuracy tradeoff including substantial degradation at stronger compression. Named competitors, token budgets, and hardware-specific throughput ground practical claims; proposed applications remain explicitly prospective.

title: LightMem: Lightweight and Efficient Memory-Augmented Generation
writing_observation: LightMem organizes persistent memory into filtering, topic consolidation, and offline updates, connecting the architecture to latency. It usefully distinguishes total costs from purely online costs, preventing deferred computation from disappearing inside an efficiency claim.

title: BAPO: Stabilizing Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for LLMs via Balanced Policy Optimization with Adaptive Clipping
writing_observation: Defines the off-policy setting before tracing instability to gradient imbalance and clipping-induced entropy loss. The named rule creates a bridge from analysis to intervention; benchmark and model identities are specific, but comparative results omit numerical scores.

title: Every Attention Matters: An Efficient Hybrid Architecture for Long-Context Reasoning
writing_observation: Starts with total and active model sizes, then connects hybrid attention to inference savings and operator alignment to training stability. Cost and efficiency ratios are explicit, but workload conditions and reasoning-quality scores are absent.

title: DeepAgent: A General Reasoning Agent with Scalable Toolsets
writing_observation: The abstract links workflow rigidity and long-horizon errors to unified reasoning, memory compression, and token-level credit assignment. Named benchmarks and retrieval settings clarify scope, but quantitative gains are absent and the nine listed benchmarks conflict with the stated count of eight.

title: Video-Thinker: Sparking "Thinking with Videos" via Reinforcement Learning
writing_observation: A missing extension from image to video reasoning motivates use of internal grounding and captioning capabilities. Dataset construction and staged training connect the mechanism to implementation; named out-of-domain benchmarks and model-size comparisons scope evidence, but improvement magnitudes remain unstated.

title: JanusCoder: Towards a Foundational Visual-Programmatic Interface for Code Intelligence
writing_observation: Locates a data bottleneck in visually grounded coding and pairs a synthesis toolkit with unified models. Corpus size and parameter ranges are explicit; task coverage is broad, but comparisons to commercial systems omit names and measured margins.

title: ReCode: Unify Plan and Action for Universal Granularity Control
writing_observation: A human-planning analogy motivates a representational gap, and recursive placeholder functions make the proposed unification easy to understand. The same structure yields a secondary training-data contribution; universal control and efficiency claims are broad because tasks, baselines, and numerical results remain unnamed.

title: Concerto: Joint 2D-3D Self-Supervised Learning Emerges Spatial Representations
writing_observation: Uses multisensory learning as motivation, then makes the technical contribution concrete through self-distillation and cross-modal embedding. Linear-probe comparisons distinguish standalone and concatenated features; a named segmentation score anchors full fine-tuning. Additional variants extend scope beyond the central representation result.

title: InteractComp: Evaluating Search Agents With Ambiguous Queries
writing_observation: Builds the benchmark around a specific hidden assumption and a controlled ambiguity construction. Complete-context and forced-interaction contrasts make the diagnostic argument stronger than raw accuracy alone, although interpreting the failure as overconfidence requires details beyond the abstract.

title: Tongyi DeepResearch Technical Report
writing_observation: Tongyi DeepResearch presents long-horizon information seeking as a specialized task and connects training stages to synthetic data and customized environments. It distinguishes total from activated capacity, while the benchmark list provides scope but few quantitative anchors.

title: Scaling Latent Reasoning via Looped Language Models
writing_observation: Places the gap in when reasoning is learned, then enumerates latent iteration, depth allocation, and pretraining scale. Controlled experiments target an alternative explanation, strengthening the argumentative structure; cross-model performance and trace alignment are reported without benchmark-specific values.

title: Emu3.5: Native Multimodal Models are World Learners
writing_observation: Introduces a unified next-state model with explicit input-output modalities and training scale. Reinforcement learning and parallel decoding address capability and efficiency separately. A quantified image-speedup contrasts with broader world-modeling and competitor-equivalence claims that lack task-level scores.

title: Kimi Linear: An Expressive, Efficient Attention Architecture
writing_observation: A strong superiority claim leads, followed by gating and hardware-efficient transition structure as mechanisms. Activated versus total parameters, identical training recipes, cache savings, and context-specific throughput make comparisons concrete; maximum gains and broad replacement language leave typical-case limits less visible.

title: The End of Manual Decoding: Towards Truly End-to-End Language Models
writing_observation: Challenges the end-to-end label through manually tuned decoding and replaces fixed settings with token-level predicted controls. Eight benchmarks and an explicitly test-tuned oracle establish comparison scope. Instruction-based control is a distinct qualitative capability, while numerical gains are omitted.

title: Can LLMs Predict Their Own Failures? Self-Awareness via Internal Circuits
writing_observation: Poses a precise question after explaining the cost and reliability limits of external verification. Hidden-state and attention descriptors operationalize intrinsic correctness prediction. Parameter overhead and backbone sizes define efficiency scope, but accuracy and calibration improvements are not numerically reported.

title: Improving Multi-step RAG with Hypergraph-based Memory for Long-Context Complex Relational Modeling
writing_observation: HGMem motivates fragmented reasoning as a consequence of passive fact storage and uses hyperedges to represent higher-order relations. The mechanism is tied to multi-step retrieval, while broad global-understanding claims need concrete task definitions and evidence beyond benchmark superiority.

title: Recursive Language Models
writing_observation: The abstract states a long-input objective, then explains externalized prompts and recursive calls in operational terms. Context-extension scale, comparator-specific median gains, task count, cost qualification, and a smaller trained model provide multiple concrete evidential anchors without claiming full-paper verification.

title: Youtu-Agent: Scaling Agent Productivity with Automated Generation and Hybrid Policy Optimization
writing_observation: Two operational bottlenecks motivate distinct generation and optimization subsystems. The abstract carefully separates in-context adaptation from parameter training and supplies several module-specific metrics; its dense inventory is informative, although percentage units and comparison conditions vary across reported gains.

title: Youtu-LLM: Unlocking the Native Agentic Potential for Lightweight Large Language Models
writing_observation: Uses an enumerated architecture–curriculum–mid-training structure to explain native agentic capability at small scale. Context length, token count, and parameter size are precise, but deep-versus-superficial cognition language exceeds the unspecified behavioral comparisons reported.

title: Let It Flow: Agentic Crafting on Rock and Roll, Building the ROME Model within an Open Agentic Learning Ecosystem
writing_observation: An infrastructure gap motivates a three-component ecosystem, followed by a trained agent, data protocols, and interaction-level credit assignment. Trajectory count and named benchmarks give scope; the concluding claim of proof is stronger than the unquantified performance evidence shown in the abstract.

title: NeoVerse: Enhancing 4D World Model with in-the-wild Monocular Videos
writing_observation: The abstract introduces a multi-capability artifact, diagnoses two scalability bottlenecks, and connects monocular-video training to pose-free reconstruction and online degradation simulation. The mechanism is partly concrete, but generalization and state-of-the-art claims lack named datasets, effect sizes, or resource measurements.

title: K-EXAONE Technical Report
writing_observation: Presents a model inventory with total and active parameters, context capacity, and six languages. Evaluation categories and size-matched comparators establish scope, but the abstract provides no scores and offers little explanation of a distinctive technical mechanism.

title: Entropy-Adaptive Fine-Tuning: Resolving Confident Conflicts to Mitigate Forgetting
writing_observation: Builds its argument from a contrast between adaptation procedures to a named token-level conflict and an entropy gate. Model ranges and application domains supply scope, but the claimed hypothesis confirmation and retained capability tradeoff remain unquantified.

title: MMFormalizer: Multimodal Autoformalization in the Wild
writing_observation: Motivates multimodal formalization through hidden physical constraints that text-only translation misses. Recursive grounding and axiom composition specify the mechanism. A 115-sample benchmark and domain-specific model findings bound evaluation, while broad coverage of physical theories remains a stronger framing claim.

title: LTX-2: Efficient Joint Audio-Visual Foundation Model
writing_observation: Begins with the missing audio channel in video generation and explains an asymmetric, cross-attending architecture. Stream sizes and conditioning mechanisms are specific; quality and computational comparisons remain qualitative despite the explicit audiovisual scope.

title: InfiniDepth: Arbitrary-Resolution and Fine-Grained Depth Estimation with Neural Implicit Fields
writing_observation: InfiniDepth links discrete output grids to lost geometric detail, then introduces continuous coordinate queries as the remedy. Its new high-resolution benchmark and downstream view-synthesis test provide complementary evidence for representation quality and practical usefulness.

title: Evolving Programmatic Skill Networks
writing_observation: The abstract defines the environment and skill representation before enumerating three maintenance mechanisms. Update gating and rollback make stability concerns explicit; named environments bound evaluation, while adaptation and generalization claims remain qualitative and the neural-training analogy receives little abstract-level support.

title: Thinking with Map: Reinforced Parallel Map-Augmented Agent for Geolocalization
writing_observation: Uses an overlooked human strategy—consulting maps—to motivate an agent loop, then assigns complementary roles to reinforcement learning and parallel search. A new benchmark establishes the test setting. A distance-threshold accuracy comparison against a named tool-equipped model makes the result concrete.

title: PaCoRe: Learning to Scale Test-Time Compute with Parallel Coordinated Reasoning
writing_observation: Connects context limits to parallel message-passing rounds, then explains reinforcement learning for synthesis. A named contest comparison includes both model size and roughly two-million-token compute, making the headline result's unusually large inference budget visible.

title: BabyVision: Visual Reasoning Beyond Language
writing_observation: A developmental contrast motivates a benchmark intended to isolate visual ability from language knowledge. Item count, category structure, and model–human scores give the gap specificity; age comparisons are rhetorically vivid, while sampling and human-evaluation details remain outside the abstract.

title: MemGovern: Enhancing Code Agents through Learning from Governed Human Experiences
writing_observation: A memorable closed-world diagnosis motivates transforming fragmented human experience into retrievable memory. Experience-card count and a named software benchmark quantify artifact scale and benefit; the percentage improvement lacks an explicit baseline or clear percentage-point versus relative interpretation.

title: Watching, Reasoning, and Searching: A Video Deep Research Benchmark on Open Web for Agentic Video Reasoning
writing_observation: Derives the benchmark from a mismatch between local video clues and web-distributed answers. Annotation scope and two agent paradigms organize evaluation. The central finding is conditional rather than celebratory: agentic gains depend on preserving anchors, with drift identified as a bottleneck.

title: Controlled Self-Evolution for Algorithmic Code Optimization
writing_observation: Maps three search inefficiencies to diversified initialization, feedback-guided evolution, and reusable memory. This parallel structure makes component motivation legible; one named benchmark and multiple backbones define scope, while efficiency and superiority lack measured magnitudes.

title: Your Group-Relative Advantage Is Biased
writing_observation: Identifies an underexamined estimator property and states the direction of bias separately for difficult and easy prompts. The correction follows directly from that diagnosis, and integration into multiple variants adds scope; no numerical improvement or theoretical assumptions appear in the abstract.

title: Rewarding the Rare: Uniqueness-Aware RL for Creative Problem Solving in LLMs
writing_observation: Distinguishes first-sample success from rollout diversity and identifies the level of regularization as the gap. Strategy clustering and inverse-frequency rewards provide a direct remedy; evaluation names sampling-based measures but supplies no numerical gains.

title: Motion Attribution for Video Generation
writing_observation: Motive frames motion attribution as a measurement gap and isolates dynamics from appearance through its objective. Data selection then becomes a downstream use of that measurement, with automated motion metrics and human preference offering complementary evidence.

title: MAXS: Meta-Adaptive Exploration with LLM Agents
writing_observation: Pairs two failure modes with lookahead scoring and trajectory stopping, explaining both quality and cost mechanisms. Naming models and dataset counts makes coverage concrete, but the claim of simultaneous performance and inference gains omits numerical tradeoff measurements.

title: A^3-Bench: Benchmarking Memory-Driven Scientific Reasoning via Anchor and Attractor Activation
writing_observation: Frames the gap in what reasoning benchmarks measure, then introduces annotated problems and a named utilization index. The construction sequence is clear, but anchors and attractors remain operationally ambiguous and the abstract reports no validation magnitude or reliability evidence.

title: Collaborative Multi-Agent Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning
writing_observation: MATTRL starts from costly, unstable multi-agent training but proposes inference-time textual experience reuse without weight tuning. Its abstract distinguishes multi-agent and single-agent baselines; precise terminology is needed so test-time adaptation is not mistaken for gradient-based reinforcement learning.

title: STEP3-VL-10B Technical Report
writing_observation: Organizes the model report around pretraining, post-training, and test-time reasoning, with concrete token and iteration counts. Named large-model comparisons and four benchmark scores create specificity; the efficiency framing needs cost context because test-time compute is explicitly increased.

title: DeepResearchEval: An Automated Framework for Deep Research Task Construction and Agentic Evaluation
writing_observation: Enumerates task-construction, evaluation-rubric, and fact-verification gaps, then mirrors them with filtered persona tasks and two evaluation components. The abstract clearly specifies a framework but ends without an empirical validation result or reliability measurement.

title: FlowAct-R1: Towards Interactive Humanoid Video Generation
writing_observation: Frames a fidelity-versus-responsiveness tradeoff, then connects chunkwise diffusion and self-forcing to streaming consistency. Frame rate, resolution, and first-frame latency provide concrete system evidence. Behavioral realism and style generalization remain qualitative claims without explicit evaluation magnitudes.

title: Urban Socio-Semantic Segmentation with Vision-Language Reasoning
writing_observation: Contrasts physically defined objects with socially defined urban categories, making the semantic gap immediately understandable. A multimodal dataset and staged reasoning system jointly address it. Reinforcement learning explains optimization, but improvement and zero-shot claims have no numerical magnitudes in the abstract.

title: Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models
writing_observation: The agentic-reasoning survey organizes environmental complexity separately from in-context and post-training methods. That cross-cutting taxonomy helps prevent mechanisms, learning regimes, and application domains from being mixed into one flat list of related work.

title: Being-H0.5: Scaling Human-Centric Robot Learning for Cross-Embodiment Generalization
writing_observation: Being-H0.5 links embodiment heterogeneity to a shared action representation and human interaction data. The abstract separates dataset scale, architecture, sensory robustness, and control latency, then uses simulated and real-platform evaluations to address different transfer claims.

title: HERMES: KV Cache as Hierarchical Memory for Efficient Streaming Video Understanding
writing_observation: States a three-way streaming requirement: accuracy, responsiveness, and memory. Attention analysis motivates hierarchical cache reuse rather than auxiliary query-time work. Time-to-first-token, token reduction, and bounded dataset gains separately support the efficiency and quality narrative.

title: The Flexibility Trap: Why Arbitrary Order Limits Reasoning Potential in Diffusion Language Models
writing_observation: The abstract begins with an appealing intuition, reverses it through an observed exploration failure, and derives a simpler training method. Retained parallel decoding answers a likely objection, while a named benchmark score supplies specificity; cautious scope appears in the initial reasoning-task claim.

title: Qwen3-TTS Technical Report
writing_observation: Leads with controllable multilingual speech capabilities, then explains architecture through two tokenizer designs and streaming requirements. Training hours, languages, and first-packet latency provide specificity; benchmark quality claims remain unquantified despite named evaluation suites.

title: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
writing_observation: EvoCUA makes static-data limitations the motivation and connects task synthesis, executable validation, and iterative policy updates. It includes both successful and failed trajectories in the learning story, while scale-generalization claims require comparisons beyond the headline OSWorld score.

title: LLM-in-Sandbox Elicits General Agentic Intelligence
writing_observation: Separates environment-enabled capability from additional training, then introduces a training extension for weaker models. Domain breadth and maximum gains motivate the contribution, but the closing general-intelligence claim is wider than the benchmark-based behavioral evidence.

title: LongCat-Flash-Thinking-2601 Technical Report
writing_observation: LongCat-Flash-Thinking links agentic robustness to environment scaling, asynchronous training, and explicit noise modeling. It separates a heavier inference mode from the main training recipe, making robustness and test-time resource growth distinct claims that need controlled evaluation.

title: SWE-Pruner: Self-Adaptive Context Pruning for Coding Agents
writing_observation: Identifies fixed pruning metrics as a poor match for task-dependent code understanding. Explicit goals and a small learned line selector make adaptation tangible. Token-reduction ranges, benchmark names, and a separate single-turn compression result distinguish evidence across usage regimes.

title: Can LLMs Clean Up Your Mess? A Survey of Application-Ready Data Preparation with LLMs
writing_observation: Defines the practical task, motivates a methodological transition, and gives a three-part taxonomy rather than proposing one algorithm. Literature coverage and evaluation analysis substantiate survey scope. Costs, hallucinations, and weak evaluation are integrated into the roadmap instead of omitted from the narrative.

title: daVinci-Dev: Agent-native Mid-training for Software Engineering
writing_observation: Links weak coding-agent preparation to a mismatch between static data and interactive workflows. Two trajectory types distinguish coverage from execution authenticity. A named benchmark, aligned scaffold, token budget, and resolution rates make the comparison concrete; the retrieved abstract ends mid-sentence.
issue: The retrieved arXiv abstract itself ends with an ellipsis; observation covers all available author-abstract text only.

title: AgentDoG: A Diagnostic Guardrail Framework for AI Agent Safety and Security
writing_observation: Turns a diagnosis-transparency gap into a where–how–what taxonomy, then links taxonomy, benchmark, and guardrail. Model families and sizes bound the release, while root-cause and state-of-the-art claims lack example diagnoses, numerical accuracy, or identified evaluation conditions.

title: Innovator-VL: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Scientific Discovery
writing_observation: The abstract organizes its argument into three contributions: reproducibility, data efficiency, and generalization. A sample-count ceiling gives the efficiency claim one concrete anchor, but named benchmarks, comparator budgets, and performance magnitudes are absent despite strong conclusions about principled data selection.

title: Advancing Open-source World Models
writing_observation: LingBot-World's abstract is a capability-oriented release statement, listing fidelity, temporal continuity, and interactivity. Latency and frame rate provide one concrete operating point, while broad environment coverage and memory claims need explicit benchmarks and failure analysis elsewhere.

title: DeepSeek-OCR 2: Visual Causal Flow
writing_observation: Questions fixed raster ordering through a perception analogy and proposes semantic token reordering before language interpretation. The abstract is framed as architectural exploration; it supplies no quantitative evaluation and appropriately describes broader reasoning potential as prospective.

title: Harder Is Better: Boosting Mathematical Reasoning via Difficulty-Aware GRPO and Multi-Aspect Question Reformulation
writing_observation: MathForge diagnoses hard-question underweighting in both optimization and data, then assigns one component to each cause. The abstract explains their interaction as a training loop, making separate and combined ablations necessary to substantiate the claimed synergy.

title: Idea2Story: An Automated Pipeline for Transforming Research Concepts into Complete Scientific Narratives
writing_observation: The abstract traces cost and reliability problems to repeated online literature processing, then explains an offline knowledge-graph alternative. Its procedural description is detailed, and evidence is explicitly called preliminary; the final scalable-reliability implication is broader than the qualitative results reported.

title: Scaling Embeddings Outperforms Scaling Experts in Language Models
writing_observation: Frames embedding growth as an alternative to expert scaling and carefully limits superiority to identified regimes. Parameter accounting and a concrete model instantiate the analysis; performance and inference-speed claims omit numerical comparisons.

title: DynamicVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
writing_observation: Defines dynamic manipulation through latency, anticipation, and control requirements, then maps those demands to three designs. Model and dataset scale are concrete, but the conclusion's response-speed and cross-embodiment claims lack numerical outcomes and explicit tested boundaries.

title: FIPO: Eliciting Deep Reasoning with Future-KL Influenced Policy Optimization
writing_observation: FIPO links coarse trajectory rewards to token-level credit assignment, then introduces future-divergence weighting. Its evaluation distinguishes peak from converged accuracy and reports longer reasoning traces, an important reminder to disclose selection and inference-compute effects together.

title: Lingshu-Cell: A generative cellular world model for transcriptome modeling toward virtual cells
writing_observation: Lingshu-Cell motivates generative state distributions rather than static embeddings and connects discrete diffusion to sparse transcriptomic data. Evaluation separates distributional realism from perturbation prediction and uses novel identity–perturbation combinations to give generalization a concrete meaning.

title: DataFlex: A Unified Framework for Data-Centric Dynamic Training of Large Language Models
writing_observation: Identifies fragmented implementations as a reproducibility and comparison problem. Shared abstractions unify three data-optimization paradigms while retaining a known training stack. Named models, datasets, and token budgets specify evaluation, though accuracy and runtime improvements lack numeric magnitudes.

title: LongCat-Next: Lexicalizing Modalities as Discrete Tokens
writing_observation: The abstract critiques language-centric attachment architectures and responds with a shared discrete representation and tokenizer. This creates a clear architectural through-line across modalities, but broad claims of reconciling understanding and generation lack named benchmark scores or explicit operating limits.

title: CARLA-Air: Fly Drones Inside a CARLA World -- A Unified Infrastructure for Air-Ground Embodied Intelligence
writing_observation: CARLA-Air defines a systems integration problem through synchronization and domain fragmentation, then specifies shared physics, APIs, and sensors. Its contribution is infrastructure compatibility and coherence; claims about supported workloads require demonstrated use cases, not only an application list.

title: GEMS: Agent-Native Multimodal Generation with Memory and Skills
writing_observation: Assigns distinct roles to loop, memory, and skills, making an agent wrapper's mechanism accessible. Task counts and a named small-model crossover illustrate breadth and potential, although gains remain unquantified and the headline comparison represents a singled-out benchmark.

title: LIBERO-Para: A Diagnostic Benchmark and Metrics for Paraphrase Robustness in VLA Models
writing_observation: Identifies instruction-form overfitting and builds a controlled benchmark varying actions and object names independently. Percentage-point drops and failure-location proportions make the diagnosis concrete. A difficulty-aware metric follows from a stated weakness in binary success rate, linking evaluation design to observed behavior.

title: Terminal Agents Suffice for Enterprise Automation
writing_observation: Uses a necessity question to challenge architectural complexity, then presents terminal-and-filesystem access as a minimal alternative. The hypothesis is crisp, but systems, task counts, cost ratios, and outcomes are unnamed, leaving the prescriptive conclusion more specific than its abstract evidence.

title: The Latent Space: Foundation, Evolution, Mechanism, Ability, and Outlook
writing_observation: The survey motivates latent computation through four limitations of verbal computation, then uses a five-part roadmap and separate mechanism/capability taxonomies. Explicit scope distinctions help prevent conceptual ambiguity; the abstract supplies no literature-selection procedure or quantitative coverage boundary.

title: Adam's Law: Textual Frequency Law on Large Language Models
writing_observation: Introduces textual frequency as an underexamined factor and explains estimation, paraphrasing, distillation, and curriculum training. Task families and a curated dataset establish scope, but the law-like framing is stronger than the abstract's unspecified experimental effects.

title: SKILL0: In-Context Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Skill Internalization
writing_observation: A three-part critique of runtime skills motivates a direct internalization question. Progressive context withdrawal and helpfulness-based retention explain the curriculum, while task-specific gains and a per-step context bound make benefits concrete; improvement units and comparative training costs remain underspecified.

title: Generative World Renderer
writing_observation: Generative World Renderer links rendering transfer to realism and temporal coherence in training data. It specifies synchronized capture channels and adds human-correlated evaluation where ground truth is absent, distinguishing dataset utility from validation of the assessment protocol.

title: GrandCode: Achieving Grandmaster Level in Competitive Programming via Agentic Reinforcement Learning
writing_observation: Uses live competition conditions as the central evidential distinction and names contest dates and repeated first-place finishes. The mechanism is summarized in two factors; the conclusion extrapolates from three competitions to a broader claim about the strongest human programmers.

title: Self-Distilled RLVR
writing_observation: Uses the contrast between dense distillation signals and sparse verifiable rewards to motivate a hybrid. Separating update magnitude from direction makes the mechanism memorable and addresses the diagnosed leakage, but claims about stability and convergence lack experimental scope or values.

title: InCoder-32B-Thinking: Industrial Code World Model for Thinking
writing_observation: A domain-specific shortage of expert reasoning traces motivates error-driven synthesis and an execution-predicting world model. Toolchain validation connects data construction to reliability, and general-versus-industrial benchmark counts plus named scores make evidence specific; causal-modeling claims receive less direct abstract-level support.

title: OpenWorldLib: A Unified Codebase and Definition of Advanced World Models
writing_observation: A definitional gap motivates both a conceptual framework and reusable inference infrastructure. The abstract explicitly states the proposed world-model criteria, clarifying its organizing lens; however, implementation coverage, interoperability evidence, and efficiency measurements are absent from the claimed unification.

title: MinerU2.5-Pro: Pushing the Limits of Data-Centric Document Parsing at Scale
writing_observation: Uses shared cross-model failures as diagnostic evidence for a data bottleneck. Keeping architecture fixed strengthens the argument for data and training contributions. Dataset growth, a revised evaluation protocol, and an absolute score gain make the result concrete, while protocol changes need careful comparison.

title: TriAttention: Efficient Long Reasoning with Trigonometric KV Compression
writing_observation: Traces a cache-compression failure to positional rotation, then explains how a geometric observation yields the scoring mechanism. Benchmark, generation length, and quality–efficiency alternatives make the evidence unusually concrete; deployment feasibility is illustrated rather than universally asserted.

title: Video-MME-v2: Towards the Next Stage in Benchmarks for Comprehensive Video Understanding
writing_observation: Connects benchmark saturation to a hierarchical construct and a stricter scoring rule, then details annotation effort. The subtitle-dependent reversal supplies a useful boundary, while 'authoritative' positioning and reasoning-validity claims require more than the listed quality-control scale.

title: Claw-Eval: Toward Trustworthy Evaluation of Autonomous Agents
writing_observation: Claw-Eval connects opaque scoring to missed safety and robustness failures, then records multiple evidence channels. Its abstract distinguishes completion from reliability across trials and uses changed rankings to motivate multidimensional evaluation rather than a single leaderboard number.

title: Rethinking Generalization in Reasoning SFT: A Conditional Analysis on Optimization, Data, and Model Capability
writing_observation: The abstract replaces a binary narrative with three interacting conditions and a temporal dip-and-recovery pattern. It closes with an explicit reasoning–safety tradeoff, making the boundary central; concrete experimental models, dataset identities, and numerical magnitudes are nevertheless absent.

title: FORGE:Fine-grained Multimodal Evaluation for Manufacturing Scenarios
writing_observation: Motivates a domain benchmark through evaluation mismatch and scarce fine-grained manufacturing data. Eighteen models and three tasks establish scope. A surprising knowledge bottleneck gives analytical value; a relative fine-tuning gain is explicitly described as preliminary evidence on held-out scenarios.

title: GameWorld: Towards Standardized and Verifiable Evaluation of Multimodal Game Agents
writing_observation: Turns interface heterogeneity and heuristic scoring into a benchmark design rationale. Two action interfaces, game/task counts, and state-based metrics specify the contract; repeated reruns strengthen the reproducibility story, although human-gap and robustness claims lack reported magnitudes.

title: HY-Embodied-0.5: Embodied Foundation Models for Real-World Agents
writing_observation: Defines embodied capability gaps, then links modality-specific computation, self-evolution, and distillation to two deployment scales. Benchmark count and small-model win count sharpen the evidence, while physical-control and frontier-model comparisons remain qualitative.

title: MegaStyle: Constructing Diverse and Scalable Style Dataset via Consistent Text-to-Image Style Mapping
writing_observation: Defines dataset quality through within-style consistency, between-style diversity, and image quality, then maps these to prompt-based synthesis. Prompt counts and dataset size specify scale; encoder and transfer models demonstrate utility. Evaluation claims lack numerical gains or benchmark names.

title: ClawBench: Can AI Agents Complete Everyday Online Tasks?
writing_observation: Opens with an everyday capability question and defines a production-web benchmark through task, platform, and category counts. A final-request interception layer clarifies evaluation safety. Eight models and a concrete low success rate establish difficulty without claiming that benchmark progress ensures general assistance.

title: When Numbers Speak: Aligning Textual Numerals and Visual Instances in Text-to-Video Diffusion Models
writing_observation: NUMINA identifies object-count mismatch as a precise generation failure and separates detection from conservative guidance. Improvements are reported across model sizes while preserving temporal consistency, showing how a targeted capability claim should include checks against collateral quality loss.

title: QuanBench+: A Unified Multi-Framework Benchmark for LLM-Based Quantum Code Generation
writing_observation: Identifies framework familiarity as an evaluation confound and responds with aligned executable tasks across three systems. It specifies probabilistic acceptance, sampling budgets, and repair conditions; numerical results lead to a clear remaining-reliability limitation.

title: WildDet3D: Scaling Promptable 3D Detection in the Wild
writing_observation: Derives open-world requirements before naming separate architecture and dataset bottlenecks. Prompt flexibility, optional depth, and human-verified box construction address them explicitly. Dataset scale, prompt-specific detection scores, zero-shot results, and depth gains provide unusually well-separated evidence.

title: Attention Sink in Transformers: A Survey on Utilization, Interpretation, and Mitigation
writing_observation: Defines attention sinks before identifying a synthesis gap, then organizes the survey into utilization, interpretation, and mitigation. The structure promises a coherent research map, but coverage counts and evidence for broad downstream harms are absent.

title: The Past Is Not Past: Memory-Enhanced Dynamic Reward Shaping
writing_observation: The abstract distinguishes current-policy randomness from repeated historical failures, making memory-based reward shaping a targeted response. Representation clustering explains the mechanism, and dataset/model counts plus two pass-rate gains specify evidence; maximum effects are complemented by separate behavioral-diversity analyses.

title: RationalRewards: Reasoning Rewards Scale Visual Generation Both Training and Test Time
writing_observation: Identifies unexplained scalar rewards as an information loss and uses explicit critiques for both training and test-time refinement. Annotation recovery supplies the data mechanism; model size and data-efficiency ratios are concrete, while downstream gains are summarized qualitatively.

title: KnowRL: Boosting LLM Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning with Minimal-Sufficient Knowledge Guidance
writing_observation: Refines a sparse-reward problem into a guidance-selection problem and motivates interaction-aware selection with a pruning paradox. Explicitly separating inference with and without hints makes the results interpretable, while point differences and model scale sharpen the claim.

title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models: Phenomenology, Mechanism, and Recipe
writing_observation: Starts from unexplained distillation dynamics and organizes the analysis into success conditions, token-level mechanism, and repair strategies. Probability-mass concentration supplies numerical specificity. A closing cost and long-horizon question preserves an unresolved boundary rather than presenting the recipe as universally effective.

title: AgentSPEX: An Agent SPecification and EXecution Language
writing_observation: AgentSPEX motivates implicit control and maintenance difficulty, then states language features and execution support. Benchmark evaluation addresses agent performance while a user study addresses authoring accessibility, giving two different evidence types for two different contribution claims.

title: Seedance 2.0: Advancing Video Generation for World Complexity
writing_observation: Presents a product-generation update with input modalities, duration, resolution, and reference limits rather than a scientific gap-and-mechanism narrative. Expert and user evaluations are mentioned without scores or protocols. Concrete operating limits are clearer than the broad comparative quality claims.

title: HY-World 2.0: A Multi-Modal World Model for Reconstructing, Generating, and Simulating 3D Worlds
writing_observation: Organizes a broad system by input type, then enumerates four generation stages and separate reconstruction/rendering roles. The open-source comparison boundary is explicit; numerous branded modules and unquantified benchmark claims make the core advance harder to isolate.

title: Agent-World: Scaling Real-World Environment Synthesis for Evolving General Agent Intelligence
writing_observation: Locates agent-training limitations in realistic environments and lifelong adaptation, then separates environment discovery from self-evolving training. Benchmark count and model sizes establish scope; superiority and scaling trends are reported without numerical effects.

title: OpenGame: Open Agentic Coding for Games
writing_observation: OpenGame distinguishes playable systems from isolated coding tasks and ties reusable scaffolding and debugging to integration failures. Its benchmark separates build correctness, usability, and intent, reflecting the need for multiple evidence types when success is interactive.

title: OneVL: One-Step Latent Reasoning and Planning with Vision-Language Explanation
writing_observation: OneVL motivates the accuracy–latency gap between explicit and latent reasoning, then uses visual and language supervision to shape latent states. It explicitly removes auxiliary decoders at inference, making training-only mechanisms and deployed cost separable.

title: CoInteract: Physically-Consistent Human-Object Interaction Video Synthesis via Spatially-Structured Co-Generation
writing_observation: Names two visible failure modes before introducing two corresponding architectural designs. The training-only interaction stream and inference removal make cost semantics especially clear. The abstract specifies conditioning inputs and mechanism, but its multi-criterion superiority claim omits numerical evaluation results.

title: Tstars-Tryon 1.0: Robust and Realistic Virtual Try-On for Diverse Fashion Items
writing_observation: Organizes the abstract around four product capabilities, then attributes them to integrated data, architecture, and training. Reference-image limits, category count, and deployment scale are concrete; success and latency claims lack exact measurements.

title: LLaDA2.0-Uni: Unifying Multimodal Understanding and Generation with Diffusion Large Language Model
writing_observation: LLaDA2.0-Uni explains tokenizer, diffusion backbone, and image decoder responsibilities before discussing efficiency changes. The abstract distinguishes understanding from generation and editing, suggesting separate evaluation paths for a unified system rather than one aggregate capability claim.

title: From Skills to Talent: Organising Heterogeneous Agents as a Real-World Company
writing_observation: Frames rigid teams and session-limited learning as an organizational gap, then defines portable roles, recruitment, and a hierarchical review loop. A named benchmark includes success rate and percentage-point improvement; formal guarantees require assumptions beyond this abstract.

title: Agentic World Modeling: Foundations, Capabilities, Laws, and Beyond
writing_observation: Motivates a taxonomy through inconsistent meanings of world models, explicitly defines two organizing axes, and states literature coverage. The contribution is synthesis, evaluation guidance, and a roadmap; future capability levels are not presented as experimentally achieved.

title: World-R1: Reinforcing 3D Constraints for Text-to-Video Generation
writing_observation: Geometric inconsistency and architectural cost jointly motivate reinforcement-based alignment. The abstract specifies external feedback sources and a decoupled strategy for balancing geometry with motion; preservation of visual quality and improved scalability remain qualitative, with no named evaluations or measured costs.

title: Programming with Data: Test-Driven Data Engineering for Self-Improving LLMs from Raw Corpora
writing_observation: An absence-of-feedback diagnosis motivates a sustained software-engineering analogy that maps data creation, training, testing, and repair. Concept and reasoning-chain errors make the mechanism tangible; sixteen disciplines establish breadth, but consistent improvements and preserved general abilities are not numerically documented.

title: Recursive Multi-Agent Systems
writing_observation: Poses a focused extension question, then distinguishes a latent collaboration module from its optimization procedure. Theory and experiments are separately signposted, with benchmark breadth and cost ranges supporting the payoff; theorem assumptions remain outside the abstract.

title: GLM-5V-Turbo: Toward a Native Foundation Model for Multimodal Agents
writing_observation: Motivates native multimodal agents through the need to perceive and act across heterogeneous contexts. The report inventories training and system improvements and preserves a text-only comparison boundary, but supplies neither detailed mechanism nor numerical outcomes.

title: Dockerless: Environment-Free Program Verifier for Coding Agents
writing_observation: Identifies repository setup as a verification cost and substitutes evidence-gathering patch review for execution. AUC improvement and three downstream resolve rates provide distinct measurement layers, with baseline deltas and environment-based comparison clearly separated.

title: The Mirage of Optimizing Training Policies: Monotonic Inference Policies as the Real Objective for LLM Reinforcement Learning
writing_observation: Traces reinforcement-learning fragility to differing training and inference probabilities, then reframes the objective around deployed behavior. Candidate construction and inference-side acceptance operationalize the proposal. Two scales under high mismatch bound the experiments, while stability and reasoning improvements lack numeric magnitudes.

title: RESOURCE2SKILL: Distilling Executable Agent Skills from Human-Created Multimodal Resources
writing_observation: Explains why resource modalities contribute complementary information, then distinguishes offline skill construction from online acquisition. Percentage-point improvement, model-domain cell counts, and ablation dimensions make the evidence specific while retaining the seven-domain evaluation boundary.

title: Orca: The World is in Your Mind
writing_observation: The abstract defines a unifying prediction target and separates dense-video from event-supervised learning. Training-data scale and frozen-backbone readouts make evaluation design concrete; the initial-instantiation framing and acknowledged limitations temper breadth, although comparative improvements remain unquantified.

title: DOPD: Dual On-policy Distillation
writing_observation: The abstract introduces a named failure mode distinguishing learnable capability from inaccessible privileged information. Token-level asymmetry motivates dynamically routed dual supervision, giving the method a clear causal story; extensive superiority, robustness, and transfer claims lack numerical magnitudes or named evaluations.

title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
writing_observation: Motivates reusable neural programs through everyday tasks that resist rules and costly repeated API calls. Compiler, adapter, and interpreter roles clarify the abstraction. A named model comparison, memory ratio, and laptop throughput make local execution benefits concrete and bounded.

title: Hierarchical Sparse Attention Done Right: Toward Infinite Context Modeling
writing_observation: HiLS identifies chunk selection as the obstacle in sparse attention and makes retrieval scores differentiable through the main objective. Its abstract separates in-domain quality, length extrapolation, and conversion from existing models, each requiring different evaluation conditions.

title: Vidu S1: A Real-Time Interactive Video Generation Model
writing_observation: Leads with an interactive capability and user control, then supplies resolution, frame rate, and hardware class as concrete specifications. Implementation names replace detailed mechanism explanation. Unlimited-duration and across-all-metrics claims are very broad relative to the unspecified evaluation protocol.

title: Search Beyond What Can Be Taught: Evolving the Knowledge Boundary in Agentic Visual Generation
writing_observation: Frames visual hallucination as an evolving knowledge-boundary problem, then introduces a reproducible benchmark and corpus. Prompt/category counts and low baseline scores make the gap visible; search failure motivates co-training, whose gains remain unquantified.

title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
writing_observation: Direct-OPD motivates reuse of cheaper RL training and explains why copying the final weak model is insufficient. A checkpoint-pair policy shift becomes the mechanism, and step-matched comparisons plus hardware/time reporting anchor the efficiency claim.

title: AlayaWorld: Long-Horizon and Playable Video World Generation
writing_observation: Moves from expensive authored worlds to autoregressive interactive generation, then presents a modular development framework. Playable actions and released artifacts make the system scope concrete; real-time capability is asserted without latency or evaluation measurements.

title: RynnWorld-4D: 4D Embodied World Models for Robotic Manipulation
writing_observation: Motivates a richer world representation through the mismatch between image prediction and physical action. Joint appearance, depth, and flow generation leads to a policy head avoiding iterative denoising. Dataset scale is concrete; real-world manipulation superiority remains unquantified.

title: Accurate, Interdisciplinary and Transparent Structure-property Understanding with Deep Native Structural Reasoning
writing_observation: Starts from scientific constraints and a joint representation–reasoning challenge, then links structural tokens to inspectable evidence. Domain-specific metrics and a controlled protein setting sharpen validation; the expert-preference percentage combines favorable and tied judgments, an important interpretive boundary.

title: DeepSearch-World: Self-Distillation for Deep Search Agents in a Verifiable Environment
writing_observation: DeepSearch-Evolve makes environment determinism and verifiability prerequisites for self-distillation. The abstract separates the environment, task pool, iterative training loop, and resulting agent, then names external benchmarks to support transfer beyond the synthetic training setting.

title: Video Generation Models are General-Purpose Vision Learners
writing_observation: Uses an analogy to language-model pretraining to pose the visual-generalist question, then converts a video-generation backbone into perception. Named tasks and specialist comparators establish breadth. Data-efficiency ranges and synthetic-to-real transfer support the thesis, while universal-intelligence implications remain speculative.

title: ABot-AgentOS: A General Robotic Agent OS with Lifelong Multi-modal Memory
writing_observation: Locates the contribution above low-level control and defines an operating layer with memory and verification. A new benchmark and explicit split-isolated evolution clarify evaluation design. Initial-subset language bounds embodied findings, while separate memory scores quantify incremental improvements.

title: ABot-N1: Toward a General Visual Language Navigation Foundation Model
writing_observation: Named failure modes motivate a slow-reasoner/fast-controller decomposition with pixel goals as the shared interface. Task examples clarify generality, and arrival and success rates provide numerical evidence; sweeping assurances of interpretability and robustness are stronger than the abstract's described validation.

title: RAGU: A Multi-Step GraphRAG Engine with a Compact Domain-Adapted LLM
writing_observation: Connects one-pass extraction noise to a staged graph pipeline and motivates a smaller specialized extractor. Named benchmarks, relative improvement, and recall comparisons substantiate results, while an answer-format artifact usefully qualifies an apparent competitor advantage.

title: Read It Back: Pretrained MLLMs Are Zero-Shot Reward Models for Text-to-Image Generation
writing_observation: SpectraReward defines image-conditioned prompt likelihood as an alternative to explicit judgments and distinguishes an internal-reward variant. Evaluation varies policies, algorithms, reward backbones, and out-of-distribution tasks; the finding that larger judges are not always better sharpens the mechanism story.

title: Ring-Zero: Scaling Zero RL to a Trillion Parameters for Emergent Reasoning
writing_observation: Frames trillion-scale training as an unexplored regime and separates pipeline changes, observed stages, and trace-quality evaluation. The seven-benchmark scope is concrete, but anthropomorphic behavior labels and claims that heuristics become redundant exceed the numerical evidence supplied.

title: Function-Aware Fill-in-the-Middle as Mid-Training for Coding Agent Foundation Models
writing_observation: Builds a structural analogy between agent tool use and ordinary function calls, then turns it into a self-supervised masking objective. Corpus provenance and decontamination, multiple model scales, exact benchmark gains, and cross-pipeline checks make the transfer claim unusually specific.

title: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Know Deeply, Act Perfectly, Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
writing_observation: The abstract grounds its proposal in a named framework's cross-platform and adaptation limitations, then maps memory and skills into a staged agent design. Platform coverage and a benchmark score supply evidence, but promotional phrasing and broad transfer claims obscure comparison conditions.

title: Boogu-Image-0.1: Boosting Open Agentic Multimodal Generation via Understanding under a Minimal Budget
writing_observation: Frames open multimodal generation around system-level understanding improvements, then names encoder, rewriting, data, and inference scaling. Image count and an explicitly theoretical training-cost estimate are specific; comparative quality is described without benchmark scores.

title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable,Navigable, and Editable
writing_observation: Locates the bottleneck at behavior-to-code mapping, carefully distinguishing it from general repository search. Representation and navigation mechanisms directly answer that gap; two repositories bound the evidence, and difficult-case gains are described without numerical effect sizes.

title: SEED: Self-Evolving On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
writing_observation: SEED turns sparse outcome supervision into a training-time hindsight signal, carefully describing trajectory analysis and action rescoring. The abstract connects evolving skills to the current policy distribution, while generalization and sample-efficiency claims need separately defined tests.

title: VideoChat3: Fully Open Video MLLM for Efficient and Generalist Video Understanding
writing_observation: Enumerates generalization, efficiency, and incomplete openness as distinct gaps, then aligns architecture and data contributions with them. Parameter size and named datasets are specific; performance and efficiency claims across video regimes remain unquantified.

title: LongStraw: Long-Context RL Beyond 2M Tokens under a Fixed GPU Budget
writing_observation: Motivates a gap between inference and training context lengths, then explains detached prompt state and sequential response replay. Hardware, context, and memory measurements are concrete; the closing statement explicitly limits results to execution capacity, not complete training correctness.

title: DataFlow-Harness: A Grounded Code-Agent Platform for Constructing Editable LLM Data Pipelines
writing_observation: The abstract names a concrete artifact-persistence gap and matches it with typed pipeline mutations plus live platform grounding. Task count, observed pass rates, costs, and latency specify evidence; comparing both a weaker and stronger baseline makes the efficiency–reliability tradeoff transparent.

title: EvolvingWorld: An Open-Schema Framework for Co-Evolving Role-Play Agents and World Model in Interactive Literary World
writing_observation: The abstract contrasts static scenes with persistent co-evolution, then specifies coupled character/world modules and an open schema. Book, sample, snapshot, task, and metric counts give the benchmark substance; the evaluation mechanism is named, but judging validity and improvement magnitudes remain unspecified.

title: TimeLens2: Generalist Video Temporal Grounding with Multimodal LLMs
writing_observation: TimeLens2 defines temporal grounding as a variable-size interval-set problem and makes supervision and reward design follow that representation. It reports size-matched and backbone-relative comparisons, while the new dataset and reward require independent attribution.

title: RynnBrain 1.1: Towards More Capable and Generalizable Embodied Foundation Model
writing_observation: Introduces a model family through embodied capabilities and explicitly distinguishes additions from the prior version. Cross-embodiment action representation connects the foundation model to robot deployment. Named benchmarks and robots provide scope, but comparative gains and real-world success rates remain unquantified.

title: Generative World Renderer at the Speed of Play
writing_observation: Clearly separates rendering from world dynamics before identifying runtime as the remaining bottleneck. Before–after frame rates and a playable-system endpoint make the improvement tangible; unbounded stream processing is presented separately from preservation and stability evaluations.

title: ABot-World-0: Infinite Interactive World Rollout on a Single Desktop GPU
writing_observation: Combines data quality, long-rollout training, control, and deployment into an end-to-end systems story. Resolution, frame rate, latency, GPU, and memory provide unusually concrete operating conditions; the abstract's measured long-horizon wording is more bounded than the title's infinity claim.

title: AREX: Towards a Recursively Self-Improving Agent for Deep Research
writing_observation: Derives the two-loop architecture from discovery–verification asymmetry, giving a strong rationale for iterative research. Context state and sparse-reward handling are explained before model sizes and benchmarks, but the final comparative gains remain qualitative.

title: Progress Reward Modeling for Robotic Learning: A Comprehensive Survey
writing_observation: The progress-reward survey begins with what terminal rewards cannot explain, then organizes interface, mechanism, and validation as linked layers. This reader-oriented sequence clarifies what a model receives, what it predicts, and what benchmark results can actually establish.

title: JarvisHub: An Open Harness for Canvas-Native Multimodal Creative Agents
writing_observation: JarvisHub motivates loss of evolving creative project state and gives the canvas several explicit system roles. The abstract is architectural and interface-focused, with no empirical evaluation claim; its design argument should not be mistaken for demonstrated productivity improvement.

title: From RLVR to RLSVR: Task Transformation Induces Self-Verifiable Rewards for Open-Ended LLM Self-Improvement
writing_observation: Explains why conventional verifiable rewards do not transfer, then separates a general task-transformation paradigm from its game-based instance. The proxy-to-quality connection is crucial but asserted rather than measured in the abstract; task coverage is named while gains remain qualitative.

title: A New Role for Relevance: Guiding Corpus Interaction in Agentic Search
writing_observation: Defines relevance before contrasting document selection with fine-grained corpus interaction. Three coarse-to-fine interventions explain how ranking informs execution; the claimed accuracy–efficiency improvement has no numerical frontier or benchmark names in the abstract.

title: From Proprietary to Open-Source: Bridging the Distribution Gap via Multi-Agent Protocol Distillation in Agentic Search
writing_observation: Explains why both hidden logits and stylistic imitation obstruct proprietary-to-open distillation. A normalized JSON protocol and privileged training branch address those constraints. Seven QA benchmarks and model-specific average success rates make evidence concrete; teacher-generalization claims are broader than the numbers shown.

title: Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance in On-Policy Diffusion Distillation
